games.summaryZh: 生成一款可在 800×600 画框中直接游玩的太空俯视角射击游戏：包含完整菜单、暂停、关卡和结算流程，支持移动、自动或手动射击、多类敌人、道具增益、碰撞反馈、视差背景、小地图及持续更新的 HUD，并保证各类战斗状态和边界行为可被稳定触发与观察。

requirements.zh: The game page has finished its initial load and setup → The game shows the menu screen with a visible PLAY button.
The PLAY button is activated while the menu screen is showing → The menu screen is replaced by the active gameplay view.

The active gameplay scene is rendered → The playfield shows a dark layered space background with star points, grid lines, a radial dark vignette, and horizontal scanline bands behind the entities and HUD.

The gameplay view is first rendered for a newly reset run → The HUD SCORE value reads 000000, the PROGRESS bar has no filled segment extending from its left edge, and a level notification showing 01 is visible in the gameplay view.
The initial gameplay instruction display timer is active during gameplay rendering → Instruction text is visible over the gameplay view.
The gameplay viewport position changes during active play → The background star and grid layers shift their positions relative to the fixed 800-by-600 viewport while the HUD remains fixed in place.
The pause key is pressed during active gameplay → The gameplay view changes to the paused view with PAUSED text over the frozen gameplay image.
The paused view has been entered from active gameplay → The paused view shows the frozen gameplay image with PAUSED text and visible RESUME and MENU buttons.
The RESUME button is activated while the paused view is showing → The paused overlay is removed and active gameplay is shown again.
The MENU button is activated from the paused screen and the return-to-menu confirmation is accepted → The game returns to the menu screen with the PLAY button visible.
The Up movement input is held while the player ship is alive during active gameplay → The player ship's position shifts upward in the playfield on subsequent frames while the input remains held.

The Down movement input is held while the player ship is alive during active gameplay and the Up movement input is not held → The player ship's position shifts downward in the playfield on subsequent frames while the input remains held.
The Left movement input is held while the player ship is alive during active gameplay → The player ship's position shifts leftward in the playfield on subsequent frames while the input remains held.

The Right movement input is held while the player ship is alive during active gameplay and the Left movement input is not held → The player ship's position shifts rightward in the playfield on subsequent frames while the input remains held.
The player ship reaches the right boundary of the playfield while alive → The player ship remains fully inside the playfield with its right edge aligned to the playfield boundary.
The weapon cooldown has completed during active gameplay while autofire is enabled and triple shot is not active → One bullet line segment originates from the player ship and travels away from it.

The weapon cooldown has completed during active gameplay while autofire is disabled, the mouse button is held, and triple shot is not active → One bullet line segment originates from the player ship and travels away from it.
The weapon cooldown has completed during active gameplay while triple shot is active → Three bullet line segments originate from the player ship in a spread pattern.
The weapon cooldown has completed during active gameplay while the fast-shot powerup is active and firing is accepted → A non-white bullet line segment originates from the player ship.
The weapon cooldown has completed during active gameplay after the triple-shot powerup timer has expired and firing is accepted → Exactly one bullet line segment originates from the player ship.
A non-piercing bullet collides with an enemy during active gameplay → The bullet line disappears after the impact and hit particle effects appear at the enemy.
A piercing bullet collides with an enemy it has not already hit before reaching its hit limit → Hit particle effects appear at the enemy and the bullet line continues past the impact point.
A piercing bullet collides with its fourth distinct enemy during active gameplay → Hit particle effects appear at the enemy and the bullet line disappears after the impact.

A bullet collides with a visible enemy and the enemy remains alive after the hit → Hit particle effects appear at the enemy, the enemy flashes, and a health bar is shown above the enemy with a filled segment that does not span the full background bar width.

A non-spawning enemy is destroyed during active gameplay → The destroyed enemy is absent from the playfield, an explosion effect appears at its position, and within the next rendered gameplay frame the SCORE display changes from its pre-destruction six-digit value to a six-digit value with a greater numeric value.

A spawning enemy is destroyed during active gameplay → The destroyed enemy is absent from the playfield, an explosion effect appears at its position, within the next rendered gameplay frame the SCORE display changes from its pre-destruction six-digit value to a six-digit value with a greater numeric value, and four smaller circular enemies appear around that position.
A visible enemy with spawning capability completes its spawn interval during active gameplay → A new enemy appears at the spawning enemy's position.
An enemy is spawned from the top edge of the playfield → A circular enemy appears along the top boundary and moves downward into the playfield.
A visible enemy of the orbiting type updates during active gameplay → The enemy's position changes around the player ship on successive gameplay frames.
A visible enemy of the grower type updates during active gameplay → The enemy circle expands outward from its center on successive gameplay frames.
A visible enemy of the direct-homing type updates during active gameplay → The enemy circle moves along a path toward the player ship on successive gameplay frames.
A visible enemy of the random-direction type updates during active gameplay → The enemy circle moves along a straight path on successive gameplay frames.
A visible enemy of the wavering homing type updates during active gameplay → The enemy advances toward the player ship along a path that bends side-to-side on successive gameplay frames.
A powerup drop is generated after an enemy is destroyed → A rectangular powerup item appears at the destroyed enemy's position.

A powerup item is visible during gameplay rendering → The item is drawn as a rectangular box with a black outer border, a gray inner border, a dark interior, colored label text, and a translucent highlight across the upper half.

A living player ship collects a powerup item → The powerup item disappears, collection particle effects appear at the item position, and the corresponding powerup indicator in the HUD shows an active timer bar.
A powerup timer is active during gameplay HUD rendering → The corresponding powerup label is drawn in bright white and a horizontal timer bar is visible to the right of that label.
A powerup timer reaches zero during gameplay → The corresponding HUD powerup timer bar is no longer drawn for that powerup label.

A health powerup timer is active while the player health bar is not full → The filled portion of the player health bar extends to the right during successive gameplay frames until it reaches the full bar width or the timer ends.
A slow-enemies powerup timer is active during gameplay → A translucent blue overlay covers the gameplay view and visible enemies are drawn with a blue-tinted overlay.

The player is taking contact damage from an enemy during active gameplay → Damage particle effects appear at the player ship, and the gameplay layer is drawn at changing horizontal or vertical offsets on successive gameplay frames.

The player health bar is rendered while the player is taking contact damage and still alive → Particle effects appear at the right end of the health bar's filled portion, and the filled portion of the health bar retracts leftward on subsequent frames while damage continues.

The player death sequence begins during active gameplay → Explosion effects appear around the player ship, and the gameplay layer is drawn at changing horizontal or vertical offsets on successive gameplay frames.

The game-over screen is showing after a run has ended → The frozen gameplay image is overlaid with PLAY AGAIN and MENU buttons, and a results table displays the labels SCORE, LEVEL, KILLS, BULLETS, POWERUPS, and TIME beside the run's values.
The PLAY AGAIN button is activated on the game-over screen → The game-over screen is replaced by the active gameplay view for a new run.
The MENU button is activated on the game-over screen → The game returns to the menu screen with the PLAY button visible.

The gameplay HUD renders while the player health is full → The HEALTH label is visible beside a dark 10-pixel-high health bar whose colored filled segment spans the full background bar width with a lighter highlight across the upper half.

The gameplay HUD renders while the player health is above zero and below full health and the player is not currently taking contact damage → The HEALTH label is visible beside a dark 10-pixel-high health bar whose colored filled segment starts at the left edge and ends inside the background bar before the right edge.

The gameplay HUD renders while the current kill count is greater than zero and less than the level target → The PROGRESS label is visible beside a progress bar whose filled segment starts at the left edge and ends inside the background bar before the right edge.

The active game reaches the kill threshold for advancing from the current level to the next level → A level notification appears in the gameplay view showing the new level number, and the PROGRESS bar is reset with no filled segment extending from its left edge.

The minimap is rendered during active gameplay → A rectangular minimap with a visible border is shown on the HUD, a translucent rectangle inside it marks the current viewport, and a 2-by-2 player marker appears at the player's scaled position.
A visible enemy is within the world area represented by the minimap → A colored 2-by-2 square marker appears on the minimap at the enemy's scaled position.

games.summaryZh: 生成一款完整的元素塔防游戏：玩家可在棋盘非路径格建造、选择、升级和出售土、水、风、火四类防御塔，控制暂停、倍速和提前发波；敌人及 Boss 按波次沿路径推进，并具备元素克制、减速、生命、资源、胜负结算和清晰 HUD 等可交互、可验证的状态。

requirements.zh: The game completes initial page setup and enters its loaded presentation state → The centered tower-defense playfield and top and bottom HUD rows are visible, the fixed enemy path is visible as a connected route across darker tiles, and neither the build menu overlay nor the tower upgrade/reclaim menu overlay is visible.
Play is toggled on from the stopped state → The Play control changes to active styling with a dark #222 background and white text, and the Send Wave control is shown at full opacity.
Play is toggled off from the playing state → The Play control no longer uses the active dark #222 background styling, and the Send Wave control returns to its inactive semi-transparent appearance.

The Send Wave control is selected while the game is not playing → The wave display remains at its pre-selection value, no new enemy appears at the path entrance, and the Send Wave control keeps its inactive semi-transparent appearance.
The ×1 speed control is selected during gameplay → The ×1 speed control is visibly styled as the active speed selection, while the ×2 and ×3 speed controls are not styled as active.
The ×2 speed control is selected during gameplay → The ×2 speed control is visibly styled as the active speed selection, while the ×1 and ×3 speed controls are not styled as active.
The ×3 speed control is selected during gameplay → The ×3 speed control is visibly styled as the active speed selection, while the ×1 and ×2 speed controls are not styled as active.

A buildable empty tile on the east half of the map is selected while the build menu is closed → The build menu overlay opens beside the selected tile, and a visible selected-tile marker appears in the build menu.
The build menu is dismissed while it is open → The build menu overlay is no longer visible over the playfield.
A path tile is selected while the build menu is closed → The build menu overlay remains hidden and no tower placement menu appears over the playfield.

The earth build option is selected from the open build menu when the selected empty tile can be built on and the player's fragments are greater than the earth tower cost → The build menu overlay closes, and a green earth tower appears on the selected tile.

The water build option is selected from the open build menu when the selected empty tile can be built on and the player's fragments are greater than the water tower cost → The build menu overlay closes, and a blue water tower appears on the selected tile.

The air build option is selected from the open build menu when the selected empty tile can be built on and the player's fragments are greater than the air tower cost → The build menu overlay closes, and a yellow air tower appears on the selected tile.

The fire build option is selected from the open build menu when the selected empty tile can be built on and the player's fragments are greater than the fire tower cost → The build menu overlay closes, and a red fire tower appears on the selected tile.

The earth build option is selected from the open build menu when the player does not have enough fragments for an earth tower → The build menu remains open, and the selected tile remains empty with no green earth tower on it.

An existing earth tower on the east half of the map is selected while the tower menu is closed → The tower upgrade/reclaim menu opens beside the selected earth tower, the menu uses green earth tower accents, and a circular range indicator is visible around the selected tower.
The tower upgrade/reclaim menu is dismissed while it is open → The tower upgrade/reclaim menu is no longer visible over the playfield.
The tower upgrade/reclaim menu is open for a tower that is already at its maximum level → The upgrade button is shown as unavailable with not-allowed cursor styling and 20% opacity.

The tower upgrade/reclaim menu is open for a non-maximum-level tower when the player does not have enough fragments for its next upgrade → The upgrade button is shown as unavailable with not-allowed cursor styling and 20% opacity.

The upgrade button is selected for a non-maximum-level tower when the player's fragments are greater than that tower's next upgrade cost → The selected tower remains on its tile, one additional colored level bar is lit on the tower tile, and the tower upgrade/reclaim menu remains open.
The upgrade button is selected for a tower that is not upgradable → The tower upgrade/reclaim menu remains open, and the upgrade button remains shown as unavailable.

The reclaim control is selected in the open tower upgrade/reclaim menu for an existing tower → The selected tower disappears from its tile, and within 1 second the fragments HUD numeric display shows a value at least 1 above the visible pre-reclaim value, with tolerance 0.
An existing tower is marked as having an available upgrade → Two white upgrade indicator marks appear on the tower tile wrapper.
The pointer hovers over an existing tower on the playfield → A circular range indicator centered on that tower becomes visible at full opacity around the tower.
A tower has an enemy target in range during active play → The tower turret is rendered pointing along the line from the tower center toward that enemy.

An earth tower's firing cooldown has reached its firing threshold while the tower has an enemy target in range during active play → A green earth projectile appears at the tower and begins moving toward the targeted enemy.

A water tower's firing cooldown has reached its firing threshold while the tower has an enemy target in range during active play → A blue water projectile appears at the tower and begins moving toward the targeted enemy.

An air tower's firing cooldown has reached its firing threshold while the tower has an enemy target in range during active play → A yellow air projectile appears at the tower and begins moving toward the targeted enemy.

A fire tower's firing cooldown has reached its firing threshold while the tower has an enemy target in range during active play → A red fire projectile appears at the tower and begins moving toward the targeted enemy.
A projectile is in flight while its targeted enemy remains on the playfield during active play → The projectile advances across the playfield toward the targeted enemy.

A projectile reaches its targeted enemy while the targeted enemy remains alive after the hit → The projectile disappears at the enemy's position, the enemy remains visible on the path, and a bright hit overlay appears on the enemy in the next rendered frame after the hit.

A projectile reaches its targeted enemy and the hit reduces that enemy's health to zero or below → The projectile disappears at the enemy's position, the enemy disappears from the playfield, and within 1 second the fragments HUD numeric display shows a value at least 1 above the visible pre-hit value, with tolerance 0.

An enemy receives damage and remains alive → The enemy remains on the path, and in the next rendered frame after damage the colored health indicator shows a reduced filled area compared with the immediately pre-damage frame; the baseline is the immediately pre-damage health indicator, the threshold is any visible reduction, and tolerance is 0.
A water-tower projectile damages an enemy that remains alive → The enemy gains the slow visual state while remaining on the playfield.
An enemy's slow effect has expired during active play → The enemy no longer shows the slow visual state while remaining on the playfield.
An earth enemy is activated at the path entrance → An enemy appears at the path entrance with green earth-colored borders, green highlight accents, and a green health indicator.
A water enemy is activated at the path entrance → An enemy appears at the path entrance with blue water-colored borders, blue highlight accents, and a blue health indicator.
An air enemy is activated at the path entrance → An enemy appears at the path entrance with yellow air-colored borders, yellow highlight accents, and a yellow health indicator.
A fire enemy is activated at the path entrance → An enemy appears at the path entrance with red fire-colored borders, red highlight accents, and a red health indicator.
An earth boss enemy is activated at the path entrance → A boss enemy appears at the path entrance with a 20 px square body, 6 px border, green earth-colored accents, and an outer corner frame.
A water boss enemy is activated at the path entrance → A boss enemy appears at the path entrance with a 20 px square body, 6 px border, blue water-colored accents, and an outer corner frame.
An air boss enemy is activated at the path entrance → A boss enemy appears at the path entrance with a 20 px square body, 6 px border, yellow air-colored accents, and an outer corner frame.
A fire boss enemy is activated at the path entrance → A boss enemy appears at the path entrance with a 20 px square body, 6 px border, red fire-colored accents, and an outer corner frame.
An active enemy is moving along a path segment during gameplay → The enemy advances along the current path segment and is rotated to face its direction of travel.
An enemy reaches a non-final waypoint on the path while the game is playing → The enemy reaches the path corner and then continues moving along the next path segment in the new direction.

An enemy reaches the final waypoint while at least two lives remain → The enemy disappears from the endpoint of the path, and within 1 second the lives display shows a number exactly 1 below the visible pre-exit lives number, with tolerance 0.
An enemy is on the playfield while the game is paused → The enemy stays at the same visible position on the path across successive frames while the paused state continues.
The player's last remaining life is lost → A browser alert dialog appears with the text “You lost.”.
The loss alert dialog is accepted → The game page reloads to the initial playfield view.

An active wave has queued enemies and its spawn timer reaches its spawn threshold while the game is playing → One enemy unit appears at the path entrance while previously spawned enemies remain on the path.

A wave has finished and no enemies remain on the playfield while later waves are still queued → The wave display advances to the next wave number, and enemies from the newly active wave begin appearing at the path entrance.

The first wave is sent from the initial wave state while the second wave remains queued → The wave display changes to “1 / 20”, and the next-wave preview counters show 9 earth enemies, 2 water enemies, 0 air enemies, and 0 fire enemies.

The fifth wave is sent while the sixth wave remains queued → The wave display changes to “5 / 20”, and the next-wave preview counters show 0 earth enemies, 13 water enemies, 0 air enemies, and 0 fire enemies.

The tenth wave is sent while the eleventh wave remains queued → The wave display changes to “10 / 20”, and the next-wave preview counters show 0 earth enemies, 0 water enemies, 15 air enemies, and 0 fire enemies.

The fifteenth wave is sent while the sixteenth wave remains queued → The wave display changes to “15 / 20”, and the next-wave preview counters show 0 earth enemies, 0 water enemies, 0 air enemies, and 17 fire enemies.
The twentieth wave is sent as the final queued wave → The wave display changes to “20 / 20”, and the Send Wave control is displayed as disabled.
All waves have been sent and cleared while at least one life remains → A browser alert dialog appears with text beginning “You won! Based on lives and elemental fragments left, your score is:”.
The win alert dialog is accepted → The game page reloads to the initial playfield view.

games.summaryZh: 生成一款以 HTTP 状态码为主题的公路躲避赛车游戏：包含桌面与移动端的标题、操控、暂停和结算流程，角色可在滚动道路上转向、变道和收集茶壶，并与 103、200、301、404、418、429、501 等状态码事件及道路危险产生对应的视觉和玩法反馈。

requirements.zh: The game has completed its initial page setup on a mobile device before gameplay is started → The title screen is visible with "js13kgames 2020" centered near the top, "collect teapots" centered above the middle, "for extra points" centered below it, "swipe to steer" centered below "for extra points", "jerome lecomte" centered near the bottom, and a highway scene behind the text with the hero sprite near the lower center.

The game has completed its initial page setup on a non-mobile device with a non-French browser language before gameplay is started → The title screen is visible with "js13kgames 2020" centered near the top, "collect teapots" centered above the middle, "for extra points" centered below it, "wasd/ULDR to steer" centered below "for extra points", "jerome lecomte" centered near the bottom, and a highway scene behind the text with the hero sprite near the lower center.

A keyboard key release that does not match the next Konami-code key is accepted while the title screen is displayed before the Konami-code sequence is complete → The display changes from the title screen to the gameplay screen.
A pointer release is accepted while the title screen is displayed → The display changes from the title screen to the gameplay screen.
Active gameplay has just started after game initialization → The lower-right HUD teapot counter reads "teapot 0".
Active gameplay is loaded from the initial level data → A teapot collectible is visible on the road at the start of gameplay.
The gameplay screen is rendered during active play after the road map cache has been built → The gameplay viewport is filled by tiled highway lanes with shoulder tiles along the left and right edges.
The gameplay screen is rendered during active play while the hero is alive → The hero sprite is visible on the highway viewport.

The gameplay screen is being rendered during active play → The HUD shows the text "score" at the upper left, a numeric score at the upper right, a countdown display near the top center, and a teapot counter at the lower right.
An active gameplay frame advances while vertical road scrolling is running → The highway background and road entities move downward through the gameplay viewport while the hero remains visible.
An upward keyboard steering input is accepted during active gameplay while the hero has an open path upward → The hero moves upward from its pre-input position along the playfield.
A downward keyboard steering input is accepted during active gameplay while the hero has an open path downward → The hero moves downward from its pre-input position along the playfield.
A leftward keyboard steering input is accepted during active gameplay while the hero has an open path to the left → The hero moves leftward from its pre-input position along the playfield.
A rightward keyboard steering input is accepted during active gameplay while the hero has an open path to the right → The hero moves rightward from its pre-input position along the playfield.
A leftward swipe steering input is accepted during active gameplay while the hero has an open path to the left → The hero moves leftward from its pre-input position along the playfield.

The hero is rendered during active gameplay while it has leftward horizontal movement active and is not dying or lane-redirecting → The hero sprite is drawn tilted counterclockwise relative to its upright orientation.

The hero is rendered during active gameplay while it has rightward horizontal movement active and is not dying or lane-redirecting → The hero sprite is drawn tilted clockwise relative to its upright orientation.
A leftward steering key is released during active gameplay while the hero is moving left → The hero stops continuing leftward movement from that steering input.

The hero attempts to move past the left highway shoulder during active gameplay → The hero remains inside the drivable highway area with its left edge aligned no farther left than the inner edge of the left shoulder.
The hero attempts to move past the top edge of the visible gameplay area during active gameplay → The hero remains visible with its top edge no higher than the top road boundary.
The hero attempts to move past the bottom edge of the visible gameplay area during active gameplay → The hero remains visible with its bottom edge no lower than the bottom of the gameplay viewport.

The hero crosses the left horizontal camera boundary during active gameplay while the viewport is not at the left edge of the map → The road background and road entities shift right relative to the canvas while the hero remains visible.
The pause key is accepted while active gameplay is running → Across successive paused frames, the hero, road, entities, and HUD remain in the same visible positions.
The pause key is accepted while active gameplay is paused → Gameplay resumes, with the road, entities, hero, and HUD updating again.
A 103 road entity is visible in the gameplay viewport → The text "103" is drawn below that road entity.
A 200 road entity is visible in the gameplay viewport → The text "200" is drawn below that road entity.
A 301 road entity is visible in the gameplay viewport → The text "301" is drawn below that road entity.
A 302 road entity is visible in the gameplay viewport → The text "302" is drawn below that road entity.
A 404 road entity is visible in the gameplay viewport → The text "404" is drawn below that road entity.
A 418 road entity is visible in the gameplay viewport → The text "418" is drawn below that road entity.
A 429 road entity is visible in the gameplay viewport → The text "429" is drawn below that road entity.
A 501 road entity is visible in the gameplay viewport → The text "501" is drawn below that road entity.
A 503 road entity is visible in the gameplay viewport → The text "503" is drawn below that road entity.

Active gameplay is loaded with a 503 road entity whose missing-road length is positive → A 503 marker is visible with one or more missing-road tiles aligned in the same lane immediately after the marker along the road direction.
The hero collides with a 103 hint road sign during active gameplay while not being lane-redirected → A hint message appears centered in the gameplay viewport.

The hero collides with a 301 lane-move road sign during active gameplay while not being lane-redirected → The hero begins sliding horizontally toward another lane and is drawn tilted during the slide.
A lane-redirect slide reaches its destination during active gameplay → The hero stops sliding horizontally and returns to its normal drawing size.
The hero collides with a 404 road-not-found sign during active gameplay while not being lane-redirected → A falling-road segment appears directly after the 404 sign on the road.
The hero collides with a 418 teapot collectible during active gameplay while not being lane-redirected → The teapot counter in the lower-right HUD increases by 1.
The hero collides with a 429 speed-limiting sign during active gameplay while not being lane-redirected → A centered seconds-remaining text appears in the gameplay viewport.
A scheduled falling-road spawn becomes due and the new segment does not overlap a 200 road-OK marker → A new falling-road segment appears at the scheduled road position.

The hero overlaps a falling-road segment after that segment has passed the fatal animation frame during active gameplay → The hero is drawn rotated away from its upright orientation during a death animation.
The hero collides with a missing-road gap during active gameplay → The hero is drawn rotated away from its upright orientation during a death animation.

The active game reaches the victory end condition → The display changes to the end screen showing "you arrived!" centered near the middle of the viewport, with "score" and "highscore" labels visible near the top.

The hero is dead during active gameplay update → The display changes to the end screen showing "you got lost!" centered near the middle of the viewport, with "score" and "highscore" labels visible near the top.
The end screen is displayed on a non-mobile device → The text "[space] to restart" is visible centered near the bottom of the viewport.
A keyboard key release other than the tweet action is accepted while the end screen is displayed → The display changes from the end screen back to the title screen with the title text visible.

games.summaryZh: 生成一款 360×240 像素风猫咪鱼市分拣游戏：从带可编辑关卡卡片和预设成绩的选关页进入游戏，玩家用猫爪选择鱼类、难度和速度，拾取漂流的鱼与纸票、操作数字打印机并将正确票据配给鱼；游戏还需呈现传送带、计时与计分 HUD、正确或错误判定反馈，以及逐条揭示鱼类成绩和最终百分比的结算流程。

requirements.zh: An enabled level-selection card is activated on the level-select screen. → The level-select cards are replaced through the tiled screen transition, and the gameplay level scene is shown after the transition.

A level-selection card action is activated while its action button is disabled. → The level-select screen remains displayed, the action button remains translucent, and no tiled screen transition begins.
The printer clear control is activated while the printer display is not showing 00. → The printer’s two-digit display changes to 00.
A pickupable non-drifting fish is clicked while the paw is able to pick up an item. → The fish becomes held by the paw, and the fish’s shadow is no longer visible.

A pickupable drifting fish is picked up while the paw is able to pick up an item. → The fish becomes held by the paw, its shadow disappears, and it stops independently drifting across the scene while held.
A held fish is dropped on a drop target that can host it while the paw is able to drop. → The fish is placed on the drop target, and the fish’s shadow is visible again.
A held item is clicked while no compatible drop target is under the pointer. → The held item remains held by the paw and is not placed onto the scene.
A fish is spawned during an active level. → A new fish appears in the gameplay scene.
A level tick reports a whole-second timer value during active level play. → The visible timer counter displays that whole-second value.
A level score update reports a score value during active level play. → The visible score counter displays that score value.
The active level reaches its end event. → The gameplay scene is replaced by the results screen through the tiled screen transition.
The results screen is created after a level in which at least one fish spawned. → The results screen displays the spawned fish entries in a grid, with each row containing at most eight fish entries.

The results reveal animation reaches a fish entry that is marked correct. → The fish entry becomes visible in its results grid cell, a particle burst appears around that entry, and the results score counter’s displayed digits change during the reveal.

The notebook page changes while the level has fish information for the new page. → The previous notebook page is removed, and a new notebook page is displayed with a fish illustration and scoring information for the selected page.

A fish on the belt with an attached paper ticket whose printed value matches that fish’s required score attempts scoring. → A check mark and orange ray particles appear around the fish, and the fish changes to a translucent appearance.

A fish on the belt with an attached paper ticket whose printed value does not match that fish’s required score attempts scoring. → Cross-shaped particles appear around the fish, and the fish remains fully opaque.
A fish on the belt with no attached paper ticket attempts scoring. → No check-mark or cross-shaped particle burst appears around the fish, and the fish remains fully opaque.
A fish that is not on the belt but has an attached paper ticket attempts scoring. → No scoring particle burst appears around the fish, and the fish keeps its current opacity.
The printer submit control is activated while the printer display reads 00 and no ticket is currently printing. → No paper ticket emerges from the printer.

The printer submit control is activated while the printer display shows a one-digit nonzero value and no ticket is currently printing. → The printer display changes to 00, and a paper ticket emerges from the printer carrying one printed digit that matches the display’s right digit before it reset.

The printer submit control is activated while the printer display shows a two-digit value and no ticket is currently printing. → The printer display changes to 00, and a paper ticket emerges from the printer carrying two printed digits that match the display before it reset.
A non-still drifting visible object updates while it is inside the gameplay view. → The object shifts to the right across the gameplay view.

The percentage animation on the results screen reaches its completed progress value. → The percentage line is visible as percentage digits with a percent sign, and the money line remains visible above it with partial transparency.

A level-selection fish-type toggle is activated when it is the only selected fish type on that level card. → The toggled fish type is shown in dark purple with its shadow hidden, and the level card’s action button is drawn translucent instead of fully opaque.

A level-selection fish-type toggle is activated when at least two fish types are selected on that level card and the toggled type becomes unselected. → The toggled fish type is shown in dark purple with its shadow hidden, and the level card’s action button remains fully opaque.

A level-selection fish-type toggle is activated for an unselected fish type on that level card. → The toggled fish type is shown in its regular fish colors with its shadow visible, and the level card’s action button is fully opaque.
A scoring information line is created for a nonnegative modifier value. → A plus-sign glyph is displayed with that scoring modifier.
A scoring information line is created for a negative modifier value. → A minus-sign glyph is displayed with that scoring modifier.
A pickupable paper ticket is clicked while the paw is able to pick up an item. → The paper ticket becomes held by the paw.
A held paper ticket is dropped on a fish that can host it while the paw is able to drop. → The paper ticket is attached to the fish and is no longer held by the paw.
The conveyor belt middle layer updates during active level play. → The belt’s middle surface pattern shifts horizontally to the right while the belt frame remains in place.
The back button is activated on the results screen. → The results screen is replaced by the level-select screen through the tiled screen transition.

The results screen is created after a level with a nonzero maximum score. → The results screen shows a money line containing the current results score counter, a slash glyph, the maximum score counter, and currency signs; it also shows a percentage line containing a percentage counter and a percent sign.
The level-select screen is displayed. → The screen background is filled with a repeating purple wave pattern, and level cards are shown as rounded panels with a repeating diamond pattern.
The results screen is displayed. → The screen background is filled with a repeating tan diamond pattern.
An active level scene is displayed with the table present. → A wood-patterned table area is visible in the gameplay scene.

games.summaryZh: 生成一款像素风步数限制解谜游戏：包含主菜单、选关、角色外观定制和可测试分享关卡的编辑器；玩家在带方向机关、箱子、滚石、钥匙、锁、陷阱、地洞、尖刺、开关、连锁方块与锣等元素的棋盘中移动，在十三步和最大步数规则下重置出生点、撤销或重开，并通过关卡完成反馈持续推进。

requirements.zh: The game completes initial setup with the active screen set to the main menu → The main menu is rendered with the title text “13 STEPS TO ESCAPE” and menu choices including “LEVEL SELECTION” and “LEVEL EDITOR”.
The game completes initial setup with a valid encoded level parameter in the URL → The display opens directly to gameplay showing the decoded custom level as the active board.

A transition to the level selector screen is accepted from the main menu → The level selector screen is rendered with numbered level preview entries arranged in a grid and one entry shown with a visible selection outline.

The highlighted level is confirmed on the level selector screen → The display changes to gameplay for that level, showing the level board with the player character placed at the level start position and facing downward.

The highlighted Continue menu item is confirmed on the main menu while a saved current level is available → The display changes from the main menu to gameplay showing the saved level as the active board.
The highlighted New Game menu item is confirmed on the main menu → The display changes to a character customization screen with the title “SELECT GENDER” visible.

The highlighted Level Editor menu item is confirmed on the main menu → The display changes to the level editor, showing the editor tile selector, orientation selector, “Test/Share” button, and an editable level grid.
A menu command is accepted during an active gameplay level → The display changes from the gameplay board to the main menu with the title text “13 STEPS TO ESCAPE” visible.
A reset command is accepted during an active gameplay level → The current level is redrawn in its initial layout, and the player character is placed at the level start position facing downward.

A downward menu-navigation command is accepted on the main menu while a menu item above another item is selected → The highlighted main-menu selection moves from its previous menu item to the next menu item below it.

An upward menu-navigation command is accepted on the main menu while a menu item below another item is selected → The highlighted main-menu selection moves from its previous menu item to the next menu item above it.

A rightward level-selector navigation command is accepted while a level entry with a selectable entry immediately to its right is highlighted → The highlighted level entry moves from its previous grid cell to the grid cell immediately to its right.

A leftward level-selector navigation command is accepted while a level entry with a selectable entry immediately to its left is highlighted → The highlighted level entry moves from its previous grid cell to the grid cell immediately to its left.

A downward level-selector navigation command is accepted while a level entry with a selectable entry in the next row is highlighted → The highlighted level entry moves from its previous grid cell to the level entry directly below it in the grid.

An upward level-selector navigation command is accepted while a level entry with a selectable entry in the previous row is highlighted → The highlighted level entry moves from its previous grid cell to the level entry directly above it in the grid.
The level selector screen is rendered with at least one completed level entry → Each completed level entry shows a star tile on its preview.

The level selector screen is rendered when the completed-level list includes every numbered level → The level selector screen shows the level grid together with the texts “CONGRATULATIONS!” and “YOU ESCAPED ALL LEVELS WITHIN 13 STEPS!”.

A level-ending condition is reached during active gameplay on a built-in level that is not the final built-in level → The display changes from the gameplay board to the level selector screen, and the selection highlight is shown on the numbered level entry immediately after the completed level.

A level-ending condition is reached during active gameplay on the final built-in level → The display changes from the gameplay board to the level selector screen, and the selection highlight is shown on the first numbered level entry.
The gameplay UI is rendered during an active built-in level → The UI shows text in the form “LEVEL: ” followed by the current level number, and the reset prompt “R: RESET” is visible.
The gameplay UI is rendered while the performed-step count is below 10 → The visible step counter text is drawn in white.

The gameplay UI is rendered while the performed-step count is 11 → The visible step counter text is drawn in yellow, and across consecutive gameplay frames the step counter text is drawn at changing horizontal or vertical positions while the level grid remains aligned.

The gameplay UI is rendered while the performed-step count is 12 → The visible step counter text is drawn in orange, and across consecutive gameplay frames the step counter text is drawn at changing horizontal or vertical positions while the level grid remains aligned.

The gameplay UI is rendered while the performed-step count is at least 13 → The visible step counter text is drawn in red, and across consecutive gameplay frames the step counter text is drawn at changing horizontal or vertical positions while the level grid remains aligned.

An upward movement command is accepted during active gameplay when the tile directly above the player is enterable → The player character moves from its current tile to the tile directly above it, and the character sprite faces upward after the move.

A rightward movement command is accepted during active gameplay when the tile directly to the right of the player is enterable → The player character moves from its current tile to the tile directly to its right, and the character sprite faces right after the move.

A downward movement command is accepted during active gameplay when the tile directly below the player is enterable → The player character moves from its current tile to the tile directly below it, and the character sprite faces downward after the move.

A leftward movement command is accepted during active gameplay when the tile directly to the left of the player is enterable → The player character moves from its current tile to the tile directly to its left, and the character sprite faces left after the move.

An upward movement command is processed during active gameplay when the destination above the player is outside the playable interior → The player character remains on its current tile and the character sprite faces upward.

An upward movement command is processed during active gameplay when the destination above the player contains a blocking tile that does not perform an action → The player character remains on its current tile and the character sprite faces upward.

An undo command is accepted during active gameplay when a completed player move is available to undo → The player character returns to the tile it occupied before the undone move, with the level board redrawn to the corresponding prior visible state.

A rightward movement command is processed during active gameplay when a pushable crate is directly to the right of the player and the tile one cell to the right of the crate can receive it → The crate moves one grid cell to the right, and the player character remains on its current tile facing right.

A movement command is processed during active gameplay when the destination contains a pushable crate and the crate has no receiving tile in the pushed direction → The player character remains on its current tile, and the crate remains in its current grid cell.
A crate finishes moving onto a switch-trigger tile → Switch tiles with the same orientation as the trigger at the crate’s destination change between their switch-on and switch-off appearances.

A crate is pushed away from a tile that contains a switch-trigger underneath it → Switch tiles with the same orientation as the trigger under the crate change between their switch-on and switch-off appearances as the crate leaves that tile.

A crate is present on a switch tile that changes into the switch-on appearance during a switch inversion → The crate on that switch tile shrinks during a removal animation until the crate is no longer visible.
A crate finishes moving onto a switch-on tile → The crate shrinks during a removal animation until the crate is no longer visible on the switch-on tile.
A crate finishes moving onto a hole tile → The crate and the hole tile at that grid cell are replaced by a filled-hole tile.

A rightward movement command is processed during active gameplay when a pushable boulder is directly to the right of the player and at least one tile to the right of the boulder can receive it → The boulder moves right along its row until it reaches the last receiving tile before the next blocked tile or border, and the player character remains on its current tile facing right.

A movement command is processed during active gameplay when the destination contains a pushable boulder and the boulder has no receiving tile in the pushed direction → The player character remains on its current tile, and the boulder remains in its current grid cell.

A boulder finishes moving with an untriggered gong-trigger tile directly in front of its stopping direction → The gong tile with the same orientation as that gong-trigger shrinks during a removal animation until the gong is no longer visible.

A movement command is processed during active gameplay when the destination contains a lock and the player has at least one collected key → The player character remains on its current tile facing the lock, and the lock tile shrinks during a removal animation until the lock is no longer visible.

A movement command is processed during active gameplay when the destination contains a lock and the player has no collected keys → The player character remains on its current tile facing the lock, and the lock tile remains visible in its grid cell.

A completed player movement lands on a key tile during active gameplay → The key tile at the player’s destination disappears from the board while the player character remains on that destination tile.
A completed player movement lands on a hole tile during active gameplay → The player character begins a respawn animation from the hole tile and returns to the current spawn tile.
A completed player movement lands on a spikes tile during active gameplay → The player character begins a respawn animation from the spikes tile and returns to the current spawn tile.
A completed player movement leaves a trap tile and lands on a tile that is not a hole without performing a tile action → The trap tile the player just left changes into a hole tile.

A completed player movement lands on a spawn tile during active gameplay → The previous current-spawn tile changes to a regular spawn tile, the destination spawn tile changes to the current-spawn appearance, and the player character stands on the new current-spawn tile.
A completed player movement lands on the current-spawn tile during active gameplay → The visible step counter changes to 0 while the player character stands on the current-spawn tile.

A completed player movement lands on a switch-trigger tile before the step limit is reached → Switch tiles with the same orientation as the trigger change between their switch-on and switch-off appearances.
A completed player movement leaves a switch-trigger tile → Switch tiles with the same orientation as the trigger change between their switch-on and switch-off appearances.

A rightward movement command is processed into a right-facing block-trigger tile during active gameplay → Block tiles connected from that trigger in the rightward direction shrink during removal animations until those blocks are no longer visible.

A movement command is processed into an untriggered gong-trigger tile during active gameplay → The gong tile with the same orientation as the gong-trigger shrinks during a removal animation until the gong is no longer visible.

A completed player movement brings the step count to the maximum allowed during active gameplay without another tile effect replacing the maximum-step respawn → The player character begins a respawn animation from its current tile and returns to the current spawn tile.
The maximum-step respawn delay completes after the player has triggered a maximum-step respawn → The visible step counter displays 0 while the player character is at the current spawn tile.
The level board background is rendered for a gameplay board → Every outer-edge grid cell is drawn with the border-tile appearance surrounding the interior board cells.
The level board background is rendered for an editor board → Every outer-edge grid cell is drawn with the border-tile appearance surrounding the interior board cells.
A mouse-wheel orientation change is accepted on the level editor canvas → The orientation shown by the editor placement preview changes from its previous direction to another direction.
A tile placement click is accepted on an empty grid cell in the level editor → The clicked editor grid cell changes to show the currently selected tile using the currently selected orientation.
A right-button tile removal click is accepted on a filled grid cell in the level editor → The clicked editor grid cell changes to an empty grid cell.
The Test/Share control is accepted in the level editor while the edited level is valid → The display changes from the level editor to gameplay showing the edited level as a playable board.
The Test/Share control is activated in the level editor while the edited level is invalid → The display remains on the level editor, with the editable level grid still visible.

A rightward option-change command is accepted on the “SELECT GENDER” character customization step → The gender selection shown on the character customization screen changes to a different visible option.
The current option is confirmed on the “SELECT GENDER” character customization step → The character customization title changes from “SELECT GENDER” to “SELECT SKIN COLOR”.

A rightward option-change command is accepted on the “SELECT SKIN COLOR” character customization step → The selected skin-color swatch outline moves to a different swatch, and the character preview changes to that skin color.
The current option is confirmed on the “SELECT SKIN COLOR” character customization step → The character customization title changes from “SELECT SKIN COLOR” to “SELECT HAIR COLOR”.

A rightward option-change command is accepted on the “SELECT HAIR COLOR” character customization step → The selected hair-color swatch outline moves to a different swatch, and the character preview changes to that hair color.
The current option is confirmed on the “SELECT HAIR COLOR” character customization step → The character customization title changes from “SELECT HAIR COLOR” to “SELECT OUTFIT COLOR”.

A rightward option-change command is accepted on the “SELECT OUTFIT COLOR” character customization step → The selected outfit-color swatch outline moves to a different swatch, and the character preview changes to that outfit color.
The current option is confirmed on the “SELECT OUTFIT COLOR” character customization step → The display changes from character customization to gameplay showing the first level board.
The UI layer is rendered while sound is enabled → A sound-on icon is visible near the upper-right area of the UI canvas.
The UI layer is rendered while sound is muted → A muted sound-off icon is visible near the upper-right area of the UI canvas.
The sound icon is clicked while the UI layer is rendered with sound enabled → The sound icon changes from the sound-on drawing to the muted sound-off drawing.
The sound icon is clicked while the UI layer is rendered with sound muted → The sound icon changes from the muted sound-off drawing to the sound-on drawing.
The menu background is rendered after its background image is available → A pixel-art background image is repeated horizontally across the visible canvas behind the menu screen.

games.summaryZh: 生成一款在草地棋盘上规划游牧聚落的路径管理游戏：玩家从菜单进入后可暂停、切换普通与删除网格、拖动蒙古包并向八个方向铺设或回收有限道路；世界会生成树木、池塘、蒙古包和牛、山羊、鱼类农场，动物成长游走，居民沿连通道路往返劳动。游戏还需呈现补充道路、农场升级、需求警告、失败结算、重新开始与返回菜单等完整反馈。

requirements.zh: The initial game presentation layout has completed setup → A grass-colored game container fills the viewport, and the SVG playfield is centered inside it.
The menu overlay reveal sequence has completed → The menu overlay shows the title "Tiny Yurts" and two buttons labeled "Fullscreen" and "Start".

The initial menu screen has completed setup with no stored highscore available → A menu overlay is visible with a button labeled "Start", and the menu text shows the tip "Tip: Left click & drag to connect yurts to" followed by "farms, or delete paths with right click."

The Start button is accepted while the menu playfield is shown in its angled zoomed-in presentation → The menu overlay is no longer visible, and the main gameplay playfield is visible in an unrotated view.
A new active game begins from the menu while the path inventory is at its reset value → The path tile counter displays "18".
The early active game reaches the score-counter reveal moment → The animal score counters are visible on the HUD.
The early active game reaches the path-tile indicator reveal moment → The path-tile indicator is visible on the HUD.
The early active game reaches the clock reveal moment → The clock display is visible on the HUD.
The early active game reaches the pause-control reveal moment → The pause control is visible on the HUD.
The pause control is accepted during active gameplay after pausing is enabled → The pause control changes from a pause-bars symbol to a play symbol while the gameplay playfield remains visible.
The pause control is accepted while gameplay is paused → The pause control changes to a two-vertical-bars pause symbol while the gameplay playfield remains visible.
The grid toggle control is accepted during gameplay when the standard grid lock is off → The standard grid overlay is visible, and the standard grid button shows a grid/hash icon.
The grid toggle control is accepted during gameplay when the standard grid lock is on → The standard grid overlay is hidden, and the standard grid button shows an A-shaped automatic-mode icon.
The red grid toggle control is accepted during gameplay when the red grid lock is off → The red delete grid overlay is visible, and the red grid button shows a delete-box icon.
The red grid toggle control is accepted during gameplay when the red grid lock is on → The red delete grid overlay is hidden, and the red grid button shows a right-mouse-button icon.
The active-game clock update reaches the January month phase while the clock HUD is visible → The clock month text reads "Jan".
The active-game clock update reaches the February month phase while the clock HUD is visible → The clock month text reads "Feb".
The active-game clock updates while the clock HUD is visible → The clock hand is shown at a different angle than in the immediately preceding rendered clock update.
The first active-game object spawn cycle creates the starting trees → Nine tree cells are visible on the playfield.
The first active-game pond spawn chooses the large-pond branch and a valid position is available → A pond occupying a 6 by 4 cell area appears on the playfield.
A pond shape is rendered on the playfield → The pond appears as a blue water area with a blurred blue shade around its edge.
The first active-game farm spawn has a valid position → A fenced farm appears on the playfield.
A newly spawned farm with a predefined starting path reaches its delayed starting-path creation moment → A short visible path segment appears connected to the farm.
A new farm is created on cells that contain visible trees → The trees inside the new farm footprint disappear as the farm appears.

The fish-farm spawn opportunity occurs after the fish-farm threshold while no fish farm exists and a large pond is available → A fish farm appears on the pond with a visible stone path segment at the pond edge.
A stone path segment is rendered on the playfield → The segment is displayed as a light gray dotted line.
A yurt spawn opportunity has a valid position → A yurt appears on the playfield with a short starting path segment next to it.
A newly spawned yurt reaches its delayed starting-path creation moment → A short visible path segment appears connected to the yurt.
A newly spawned yurt reaches its resident-arrival moment → Two person icons appear at the yurt.
A yurt rotation to a new facing direction is accepted → The yurt has a short starting path segment on the new facing side, and the previous short starting path segment is absent.
A valid left-click path drag begins while the standard grid lock is off → The standard grid overlay and hazard guide lines become visible on the playfield.
A left-click path drag begins on a non-yurt buildable grid cell during active gameplay → A path drag indicator is visible at the drag-start cell.
A valid left-click path drag update reaches an adjacent grid cell before the placement is finalized → A visible drag preview line is drawn from the drag-start cell toward the adjacent cell.
A pointer release ends a left-click path drag while the standard grid is in automatic mode → The standard grid overlay, hazard guide lines, and path drag indicator are not visible.
A delete-mode pointer drag is active over the playfield → The red delete grid overlay is visible and the standard grid overlay is hidden.
A pointer release ends delete-mode dragging while the red delete grid is in automatic mode → The red delete grid overlay and red hazard guide lines are not visible.

A left-click drag path placement is accepted between two adjacent non-yurt cells while at least one path tile remains in inventory → A new visible path segment is drawn between the previous cell and the adjacent cell, and the path tile counter decreases by 1 from its pre-placement displayed number.

A left-click drag path placement is accepted from one cell into the cell directly above while at least one path tile remains in inventory → A new visible path segment is drawn from the previous cell to the cell directly above it.

A left-click drag path placement is accepted from one cell into the cell directly above and to the right while at least one path tile remains in inventory → A new visible diagonal path segment is drawn from the previous cell to the cell above and to the right.

A left-click drag path placement is accepted from one cell into the cell directly to the right while at least one path tile remains in inventory → A new visible path segment is drawn from the previous cell to the cell directly to the right.

A left-click drag path placement is accepted from one cell into the cell directly below and to the right while at least one path tile remains in inventory → A new visible diagonal path segment is drawn from the previous cell to the cell below and to the right.

A left-click drag path placement is accepted from one cell into the cell directly below while at least one path tile remains in inventory → A new visible path segment is drawn from the previous cell to the cell directly below it.

A left-click drag path placement is accepted from one cell into the cell directly below and to the left while at least one path tile remains in inventory → A new visible diagonal path segment is drawn from the previous cell to the cell below and to the left.

A left-click drag path placement is accepted from one cell into the cell directly to the left while at least one path tile remains in inventory → A new visible path segment is drawn from the previous cell to the cell directly to the left.

A left-click drag path placement is accepted from one cell into the cell directly above and to the left while at least one path tile remains in inventory → A new visible diagonal path segment is drawn from the previous cell to the cell above and to the left.
A left-click drag connection from a yurt to a farm is completed during active gameplay → A visible path of connected tiles is drawn between the yurt and the farm.
A new path is created through grid cells containing visible trees during active gameplay → The trees in the path cells disappear as the new visible path is drawn.
A drag path placement reaches a valid adjacent non-yurt cell while the path tile counter is at zero → The path tile counter displays "!" and no new path segment appears at that placement.

A drag path placement reaches an adjacent cell that is already connected to the drag-start cell by the same path → The browser pointer cursor is shown as a not-allowed cursor and no additional path segment is drawn between those two cells.
A left-click path drag update remains in the same grid cell as the previous drag cell → No path preview segment is visible from that drag update.
A left-click path drag update reaches a grid cell more than one cell away horizontally from the previous drag cell → No path preview segment is visible from that drag update.
A right-click path deletion is accepted on an existing path during active gameplay → The selected visible path is removed from the playfield.
A left-click path deletion is accepted on an existing path while the red delete grid lock is on → The selected visible path is removed from the playfield.
A path tile is removed while the path inventory displayed count is below 99 → The selected visible path tile is removed and the path tile counter increases by 1 from its pre-removal displayed number.
A path deletion request targets a fixed yurt starting path during active gameplay → The yurt's short starting path segment remains visible during the next 0.5 seconds.

The periodic path inventory reward begins while the path inventory displayed count is below 99 → The path tile counter displays "+9" and then returns to a numeric path count during the reward sequence.

The periodic path inventory reward opportunity occurs while the path tile counter displays "99" → The path tile counter continues to display "99" and does not switch to "+9" during the next 3 seconds.
A newly spawned ox farm reaches its first scheduled animal-arrival moment → One ox appears inside the farm.
A newly spawned ox farm reaches its third scheduled animal-arrival moment → A third ox appears inside the farm.
A newly spawned goat farm reaches its first scheduled animal-arrival moment → One goat appears inside the farm.
A newly spawned goat farm reaches its third scheduled animal-arrival moment → A third goat appears inside the farm.
A newly spawned fish farm reaches its first scheduled fish-arrival moment → One fish appears in the fish farm.
A newly spawned fish farm reaches its fifth scheduled fish-arrival moment → A fifth fish appears in the fish farm.
A new ox is added to the playfield → The ox counter area is visible, and the ox counter displays a number one greater than its displayed number before the ox was added.
A new goat is added to the playfield → The goat counter area is visible, and the goat counter displays a number one greater than its displayed number before the goat was added.
A new fish is added to the playfield → The fish counter area is visible, and the fish counter displays a number one greater than its displayed number before the fish was added.

An ox update occurs while the ox has a movement target more than 1 SVG unit away, the ox's current rotation differs from the target angle by more than 0.1 radians, and the proposed movement is not blocked by another ox → The ox's rendered body position and body orientation both change between consecutive animation frames.

A goat update occurs while the goat has a movement target more than 1 SVG unit away, the goat's current rotation differs from the target angle by more than 0.1 radians, and the proposed movement is not blocked by another goat → The goat's rendered body position and body orientation both change between consecutive animation frames.

A fish update occurs while the fish has a movement target more than 1 SVG unit away, the fish's current rotation differs from the target angle by more than 0.1 radians, and the proposed movement is not blocked by another fish → The fish's rendered body position and body orientation both change between consecutive animation frames.
A farm assigns an available same-type person a route to an undersupplied farm over connected paths → A person icon leaves its yurt and travels along the drawn path toward the farm.
A person at a farm begins a return-home route over connected paths → The person icon leaves the farm and travels along the drawn path toward its yurt.
A person reaches the fish-service tick while at a fish farm → The fish bodies in that fish farm change to the orange fish color one after another.

A person begins leaving a fish farm after the service duration → The person icon leaves the fish farm and travels along the drawn path toward its yurt; the fish bodies in that fish farm change to the shaded water color one after another.
A farm warning is toggled on → A warning marker is visible on the farm.
A farm warning is toggled off → The farm warning marker is no longer visible.
An animal warning is toggled on → A warning marker is visible on the animal.
An animal warning is toggled off → The animal warning marker is no longer visible.
An ox farm upgrade is accepted while the farm has two visible adult oxen → The two adult oxen display love indicators, and one baby ox appears at the farm.
A goat farm upgrade is accepted while the farm has two visible adult goats → The two adult goats display love indicators, and one baby goat appears at the farm.
An ox farm upgrade is accepted while the farm has three visible adult oxen and fewer than five total visible oxen → The three adult oxen display love indicators, and two baby oxen appear at the farm.
A fish farm upgrade is accepted while the farm has fewer than nine visible fish → Four additional fish appear in the fish farm.

An ox farm upgrade is rejected because the farm already has at least five visible oxen → The farm's visible ox count remains at its pre-upgrade count and no love indicators appear at that farm during the next 9 seconds.
A goat farm upgrade is rejected while the farm has six visible goats → The farm's visible goat count remains six and no love indicators appear at that farm during the next 9 seconds.
A fish farm upgrade is rejected because the farm already has at least nine visible fish → The farm's visible fish count remains at its pre-upgrade count during the next 11 seconds.
A baby ox becomes an adult during active gameplay → The ox changes from baby rendering to adult rendering, and the ox horns are visible.
A baby fish reaches adulthood during active gameplay → The fish changes from baby rendering to adult rendering.
A farm warning reaches the maximum overflow threshold during active gameplay → A game-over overlay with buttons labeled "Restart" and "Menu" appears within 1 second.

The terminal game-over camera transition begins for the lost farm → The playfield is rotated and zoomed toward the lost farm, and the animal counters, clock, path-tile indicator, and pause control are hidden.

The game-over overlay content reveal sequence completes → The overlay shows the header text "Game Over", the sentence "Too few people could tend to this farm in time.", and a button labeled "Overlay On/Off".
The game-over screen is shown with the current game score available → The game-over overlay includes a text label beginning with "Score:".
The game-over screen is shown with oxen, goats, and fishes counted → The game-over overlay shows ox, goat, and fish icons, each followed by a multiplication sign and a numeric count.

The game-over screen is shown with yurt, ox, goat, and fish counts available → The game-over overlay includes a numeric text label ending with "settlers", and the number after "Score:" equals the displayed settlers number plus the displayed ox, goat, and fish counts.
The Restart button is accepted on the game-over screen → The game-over overlay disappears and the main gameplay playfield is visible again.
A new active game begins from the game-over restart flow → The path tile counter displays "18".
The Menu button is accepted on the game-over screen → The game-over overlay is replaced by the menu overlay with a button labeled "Start".

games.summaryZh: 生成一款以卡牌铺设道路的轻量冒险游戏：玩家从标题页进入棋盘，在手牌与牌堆之间选择或拖拽带四向连接、宝石和特殊效果的卡牌，沿合法相邻位置扩建路线，让角色自动穿行、得分、治疗并开启宝箱。游戏还需包含多种遗物、奖励选择、连锁移动、关卡伤害与重抽机制，以及征服庆祝、关卡扩张和失败重开等完整流程。

requirements.zh: The game canvas has completed initial DOM setup → The game is presented in a 4:3 canvas area with an 800-by-600 internal playfield against a black page background.
A normal game frame is rendered with the background visible → The background behind the cards is green with semi-transparent light diagonal tartan stripe bands spanning the playfield.

The initial page/startup screen has completed setup → A title screen is visible with the centered text "CASUAL CRUSADE" near the top, followed by "by Antti Haavikko", "Made for js13k 2023", and "Press F for full screen" near the bottom.

The initial title screen is rendering before play starts → A centered rectangular "PLAY" button is visible below the title text, with a black outer rectangle, a white inner rectangle, and black centered button text.
The first start delay completes after the title-screen start button has been accepted → Active gameplay is visible and a centered splash panel with a crusade title appears over the gameplay view.
The first active gameplay view after a new game is initialized is rendering → The play area is visible with a board and cards, the HUD shows "LIFE: 5/5", and the score readout shows "0".
The first level board is visible after a new game starts → The visible board contains five regular non-reward tile spaces, with the crusader on the starting tile.
A card whose connectors include up is rendered → The card face shows a black connector line from the center circle to the top edge.
A card whose connectors include right is rendered → The card face shows a black connector line from the center circle to the right edge.
A card whose connectors include down is rendered → The card face shows a black connector line from the center circle to the bottom edge.
A card whose connectors include left is rendered → The card face shows a black connector line from the center circle to the left edge.
A blank card with no connectors is rendered → The card face has no black connector line to any edge and no black center connector circle.
A card that contains a gem is rendered → The card face shows a colored gem circle at its center.
A card that contains a gem becomes hovered → A tooltip appears near the card showing the gem name and description text with colored highlighted words.
A closed reward chest tile is rendered → The tile shows a small chest with a black outer body, yellow front panel, black slot, and a lid resting on top.
The draw pile has a positive card count during active gameplay → A draw-pile stack is visible in the hand area with a black numeric count drawn at the center of the top card.
The draw pile count reaches zero during active gameplay → The draw-pile stack is no longer rendered in the play area.

A movable card with at least one available destination is picked up during active play → The card is shown as selected, and at least one empty board tile displays a placement highlight while the card remains selected.

A card with an upward connector is selected while an empty board tile directly below a card with a downward connector is available → That empty board tile displays a placement highlight for the selected card.

A card with a downward connector is selected while an empty board tile directly above a card with an upward connector is available → That empty board tile displays a placement highlight for the selected card.

A card with a left connector is selected while an empty board tile directly to the right of a card with a right connector is available → That empty board tile displays a placement highlight for the selected card.

A card with a right connector is selected while an empty board tile directly to the left of a card with a left connector is available → That empty board tile displays a placement highlight for the selected card.
A card is selected while a reward chest tile is nearby as a possible board space → The reward chest tile does not display a card placement highlight.
A card is selected while an empty board tile has no reciprocal connector match with any neighboring placed card → That empty board tile does not display a placement highlight.
A dragged movable card enters within 100 canvas pixels of a legal empty board tile during active play → That board tile displays a placement highlight while the card is still being dragged.
A selected movable card is placed during active play → The selected card is rendered at the placement location, and the placement highlights on the board disappear.

A movable card is released during active play while no legal board tile is within 100 canvas pixels of the card → The card returns to the hand area and no new card appears on the board from that release.

A placed card creates a connected path from the character's current tile to the placed card → The character travels along the connected cards toward the newly placed card, and each visited card changes to a pale yellow face color after the character steps on it.

A placed card creates a path that revisits a card whose gem color is currently freely revisitable → During the single path traversal, the character is visibly drawn on the same card tile at two separated moments before reaching the placed card.

A character path step after the starting tile is processed during active gameplay → The character moves from the previous card tile toward the next card tile, and a floating numeric score label appears at the stepped-on card.
A scoring event is applied during active gameplay → Within the next rendered frame, the score readout displays a number at least 1 greater than the pre-event displayed number.

A scoring event for the first path step on a yellow gem card occurs on level 1 while the score multiplier is 1 → A floating numeric label "10" appears at the stepped-on card, and the score readout increases by 10 from its pre-step displayed number.
An orange multiplier card step is applied during a path traversal → A floating text label beginning with "x" appears above the stepped-on card to show the new multiplier.

A red card is placed while the player is below maximum life → Green rectangular particles appear around the character, and the HUD life text increases by 1 in the current-life number while the maximum-life number stays the same.

A red card step is applied while the healing-on-red relic is active and the player is below maximum life → Green rectangular particles appear around the character, and the HUD life text increases by 1 in the current-life number while the maximum-life number stays the same.
A blue card is placed while the draw pile contains at least one card → The blue card appears on the board and a new card appears from the draw-pile area into the visible hand layout.
A draw-card effect occurs while the draw pile is empty → No new card appears from the draw-pile area and the visible hand does not gain a card.
A card is drawn from the deck into the hand during active gameplay → A new card appears from the draw-pile area and the hand layout updates to include the added card.
A discard effect is applied to a visible hand card → A hand card moves to the draw-pile area, and a replacement card appears in the visible hand.

A card with the blank-tile creation effect activates while it has at least one empty non-reward neighboring board tile → An expanding circular pulse appears from the activating card, and at least one previously empty neighboring board tile displays a blank card.
A blank-tile creation effect activates while an empty diagonal neighboring board tile is available → The diagonal neighboring tile displays a blank card after the effect.
A blank-tile creation effect activates while a reward chest occupies one of the surrounding board spaces → The reward chest remains visible as a chest and is not replaced by a blank card.
A level-end check finds no unlocked hand cards remaining → The current board is replaced by the next level board, with the character placed on a starting tile and cards displayed in the hand.
A level-end check finds that the playable board is full → The current board is replaced by the next level board, with the character placed on a starting tile and cards displayed in the hand.

A level-end check finds unlocked hand cards but none has any legal placement → The current board is replaced by the next level board, with the character placed on a starting tile and cards displayed in the hand.
A stuck level-end check qualifies for the once-per-level redraw effect → After a short delay, the cards shown in the hand are replaced by a newly dealt hand while the same board remains visible.
A level-end check occurs while a reward selection panel is open → The reward selection panel remains visible, and the current board is not replaced by a next-level board during that check.

A level-end damage check finds at least one empty non-reward board tile and the player has enough life to survive → The HUD current-life number decreases by at least 1 while the game-over overlay does not appear.

A level-end damage sequence processes an empty non-reward board tile → A circular pulse appears from that tile, the camera view jolts, the tile becomes hidden from the board, and the HUD current-life number decreases by 1.

A surviving level-end conquest sequence begins after level-end damage is resolved → A centered splash banner with a conquest or crusade message appears over the play area, and the character performs a hop in place.
The first level advances to the second level → After the transition, the visible board for the new level contains seven regular non-reward tile spaces.
The third level board is visible after advancing from the previous level → The visible board contains nine regular non-reward tile spaces.
