A visible mouse receives a movement update during active gameplay → The mouse's body is drawn at a different screen position on a subsequent rendered frame while its tail remains attached behind the triangular body.

A visible mouse reaches the left boundary of the game field during active gameplay → The mouse remains inside the game field at the left boundary and its subsequent movement is directed rightward into the field.
Remaining mice are off-screen to the right while no mouse is visible in the current gameplay viewport → An off-screen mouse indicator is drawn on the right edge of the gameplay view.
At least one mouse is visible in the current gameplay viewport → No off-screen mouse indicator is drawn along the edges of the gameplay view.
An off-screen mouse indicator is rendered for a mouse outside the current gameplay viewport → The indicator is drawn as a red filled triangle on an edge of the gameplay view.

The cat at ground level contacts a mouse while its inflation level is below the maximum → The contacted mouse is no longer drawn, the number following the "Mice " label in the HUD increases by 1 on the next rendered gameplay view, and within 1 second the cat's soft body outline extends outside its pre-contact body silhouette on at least one side.

The cat at ground level contacts a mouse while its inflation level is below the maximum and the stamina bar is not full → The contacted mouse disappears, and within 1 second the filled portion of the stamina bar extends rightward from its pre-contact right edge.

The cat at ground level contacts a mouse while its inflation level is at the maximum → The contacted mouse remains drawn in the play field, and the number following the "Mice " label in the HUD does not increase on the next rendered gameplay view.

The airborne cat passes through a mouse's position while above the ground-collision height → The mouse remains drawn in the play field, and the number following the "Mice " label in the HUD does not increase on the next rendered gameplay view.
The final remaining mouse of the current wave is eaten → The final mouse disappears and a popup overlay appears with a visible "Continue" button for advancing to the next wave.
A new wave is initialized after completing the previous wave → On the next rendered gameplay view, the top HUD displays a "Wave " label with the new wave number.
The next-wave popup is shown after the wave number has been advanced → A popup overlay is visible with the title text matching "Next Wave " followed by the advanced wave number.
The Continue button in the next-wave popup is accepted → The next-wave popup overlay disappears and the gameplay screen remains visible.
The cat has reached the state where it cannot eat more during gameplay → A red message appears near the top of the canvas reading "Can't eat more. Need to purge: double-tap on the cat."

A purge is accepted while the cat is inflated during gameplay → The cat's inflated body outline contracts inward from its pre-purge outline until the cat is drawn with normal uninflated body proportions, a poop object appears in the play field at the cat's purge position, and the cat leaves the ground and follows an airborne arc after the purge.
An active uncollected clover is within the current gameplay viewport when the field is rendered → A green clover symbol is drawn at the clover's position in the play field.
The cat at ground level contacts an active uncollected clover → The clover disappears from the play field, and the stamina bar fills to the full width of its outlined bar.
An active uncollected clover reaches its lifetime limit during gameplay → The clover is no longer drawn at its previous position and a clover is drawn at another position in the play field.
A poop object is within the current gameplay viewport when the field is rendered → A brown poop pile is drawn at its position with an oval shadow underneath it and small black fly sprites around it.

The cat at ground level contacts a poop while not protected from poop damage → The contacted poop disappears from the play field, and the filled portion of the stamina bar begins moving left from its pre-collision right edge.

The cat contacts a poop while protected from poop damage → The poop remains drawn in the play field, and the filled portion of the stamina bar keeps the same visible right edge on the next rendered gameplay view.

The airborne cat passes through a poop's position while above the ground-collision height → The poop remains drawn in the play field, and the filled portion of the stamina bar keeps the same visible right edge on the next rendered gameplay view.
The game-over sequence is triggered after a run ends → A popup overlay is visible with the title text "Game Over".
The game-over popup is shown after a run ends with a counted mouse total → The popup overlay displays body text matching "Your score: " followed by the run's mouse total and then " mice eaten".
The Restart button in the game-over popup is accepted → The gameplay scene is re-entered and the screen displays the heading text "Game Screen" above the play area.

games.summaryZh: 生成一款中世纪城堡建造解谜游戏：玩家使用键盘、触控或手柄移动并放置不同结构块，在有限空间和规则约束下完成城堡轮廓，支持重开、选关及清晰的合法性与通关反馈。

requirements.zh: The title screen is rendered during initial game startup → The screen shows an intro-colored title view with a left-side “START” label and a right-side “START” label with “MUSIC OFF” displayed below it.

A first mouse press is received while the initial title screen is still waiting to start the game → The display leaves the title screen and transitions to the first gameplay level with the board visible.
The first gameplay level is rendered after leaving the title screen → The playfield is visible and the centered instruction text “ARROWS TO MOVE OR TAP ON SCREEN” appears over the level.

A non-title gameplay frame is rendered → The canvas background outside the board is filled with the background color, and the board area is drawn as a solid board-colored rectangle behind pieces and grid markings.
A rendered level board has more than one column → At least one internal vertical grid line is drawn between board columns.
A rendered level board has more than one row → At least one internal horizontal grid line is drawn between board rows.
A rendered level contains a void cell → The void cell is drawn as a background-colored hole inside the board grid.
A rendered level contains a goal cell → The goal cell is drawn with a hatched target pattern inside its grid cell.
A rendered level contains a box piece → The box appears as a box-colored block with a stroked marking on its face.
A rendered level contains a cutter piece → The cutter is visible as a red blade-like block occupying its grid cell.
A rendered level contains a duckling piece that is not in the connection animation → The duckling appears as a duckling-colored block on the board.

A duck is rendered while it is not on a goal and no duck is on a goal in at least one of the current goal-state checks → The duck block is drawn with its normal duck-colored body and no diagonal X mark on its face.
A duck is rendered while it is on a goal in both the previous and current goal checks → The duck block is drawn with goal-state coloring and a V-shaped mark on its face.

A duck is rendered while it is not on a goal and at least one other duck is on a goal in both goal checks → The duck block is drawn with its normal duck-colored body and a diagonal X mark on its face.

A left movement command is accepted during active gameplay while the controlled duck can move into the adjacent board cell to the left → The controlled duck moves from its current board cell into the adjacent board cell on its left.

An up movement command is accepted during active gameplay while the controlled duck can move into the adjacent board cell above it → The controlled duck moves from its current board cell into the adjacent board cell above it.

A right movement command is accepted during active gameplay while the controlled duck can move into the adjacent board cell to the right → The controlled duck moves from its current board cell into the adjacent board cell on its right.

A down movement command is accepted during active gameplay while the controlled duck can move into the adjacent board cell below it → The controlled duck moves from its current board cell into the adjacent board cell below it.

A pointer drag with a leftward board displacement beyond the pointer dead zone is accepted during active gameplay while the controlled duck can move into the adjacent board cell to the left → The controlled duck moves from its current board cell into the adjacent board cell on its left.

A simultaneous left-and-up movement command is accepted during active gameplay while both movement steps are valid for the controlled duck → The controlled duck moves from its starting board cell to the board cell one column left and one row above that starting cell.

Opposing left and right movement commands are held during active gameplay with no unopposed vertical movement command → The controlled duck remains in its current board cell for the rendered response to the held commands, and no movement animation plays.

A primarily horizontal pointer drag remains inside the pointer dead zone during active gameplay → The controlled duck remains in its current board cell for the rendered response to the drag, and no movement animation plays.

A left movement command is issued during active gameplay while the controlled duck's target cell to the left is outside the board → The controlled duck remains in its current board cell and no board piece moves.

A left movement command is issued during active gameplay while the controlled duck's adjacent cell to the left contains a blocking piece that cannot be pushed → The controlled duck remains in its current board cell and the blocking piece remains in its cell.

A left movement command is accepted during active gameplay while the controlled duck's adjacent cell to the left contains a movable piece and that piece can move into the next cell to the left → The controlled duck moves into the adjacent cell on its left, and the movable piece that was in that adjacent cell moves one cell left into the next cell.

A left movement command is accepted during active gameplay while the controlled duck is part of a movable cluster containing another duck block and the entire cluster can shift one cell left → The controlled duck and the other duck block in its cluster move one board cell left together.

A left movement command is accepted during active gameplay while the controlled duck's adjacent cell to the left contains a movable clustered piece and every piece in that cluster can shift one cell left → The controlled duck moves into the adjacent cell on its left, and every piece in the pushed cluster moves one board cell left together.

A left movement command is accepted during active gameplay while the controlled duck pushes a chain of movable pieces that can all shift one cell left → The controlled duck moves into the adjacent cell on its left, and each movable piece in the pushed chain moves one board cell left.

A movement command is accepted during active gameplay for a non-final duck whose destination is a cutter cell → After the movement completes, that duck is no longer visible on the board and the cutter remains visible on its cell.
A movement command would move the only remaining live duck onto a cutter cell → The move is rejected; the duck remains in its pre-move board cell and does not shrink or disappear.

A movement command is accepted during active gameplay for a movable non-duck piece whose destination is a cutter cell → After the movement completes, that non-duck piece is no longer visible on the board and the cutter remains visible on its cell.
A duckling cluster becomes connected to a duck cluster during active gameplay → After the connection completes, the connected duckling blocks are rendered as duck-colored duck blocks.

A duck cluster is split into multiple disconnected duck groups during active gameplay → The group disconnected from the retained duck group is rendered as duckling-colored blocks, while the retained duck group remains rendered as duck blocks.

A level win check succeeds because the number of live ducks matches the number of goals and every duck is on a goal in both goal checks → A level-ending transition begins, with the level view covered by the intro-colored transition overlay.
A level-completion transition reaches the moment when the game enters the next level → The previous board is replaced by a new level board layout.

The reset command is accepted during active gameplay after the current level layout has been visibly changed from its starting arrangement → The current level returns to its starting board arrangement, with the controlled duck and level pieces back at their initial grid positions.
The level-select icon is activated from an active gameplay level → The current puzzle board is replaced by the level-select board.
The level-select duck reaches a goal marker on the level-select board → The level-select board is replaced by the selected puzzle level board.

games.summaryZh: 生成一款猫咪女巫冒险游戏：玩家移动、发射火球并切换季节，利用冬季结冰、夏季藤蔓、秋季蘑菇与落叶、春季花朵等环境变化寻找失踪猫咪，让季节切换与世界状态变化直观可见。

requirements.zh: The intro cinematic reaches the cat-rescue motivation panel → The on-screen cinematic text displays “MY CATS VANISHED” and “I MUST SAVE THEM!” as two text lines.
The intro cinematic reaches the season-chaos panel → The on-screen cinematic text displays “OH NO! THE SEASONS ARE IN CHAOS!”.
The intro cinematic reaches the season-orb objective panel → The on-screen cinematic text displays “FIND SEASON ORBS IN TEMPLES” and “SAVE THE CATS” as two text lines.
The intro cinematic reaches the control-instruction panel → The on-screen cinematic text displays “MOVE WITH ARROWS” and “ACTION TO INTERACT” as two instruction lines.
A non-final cinematic panel reaches its configured duration → The current cinematic text is replaced by the next cinematic text panel without player input.
The final step of a cinematic reaches its end → The cinematic text disappears from the screen and the gameplay view is shown without the cinematic dialogue panel.

A readable text panel is being rendered over the gameplay view → A black rectangular panel is drawn near the top of the gameplay canvas with an inset from the left and right canvas edges, and the readable text appears inside the panel.
The player performs the action input while facing upward toward a sign panel that contains text → A black dialogue panel appears over the gameplay view and displays the sign text in pixel lettering.

The player performs the action input while adjacent to a sign panel, with no dialogue panel open, and the character is not facing upward → No black dialogue panel is added to the gameplay view and no sign text appears.
The player performs the action input while a dialogue panel is already open → The black dialogue panel and its text disappear from the gameplay view.
The player holds an upward movement input during active gameplay while a dialogue panel is open → The character remains at its pre-input screen position and the dialogue panel remains visible.

The player holds an accepted upward movement input during active gameplay while the character is not blocked → The character’s on-screen position shifts upward and the character sprite uses an upward-facing frame.

The player holds an accepted downward movement input during active gameplay while the character is not blocked → The character’s on-screen position shifts downward and the character sprite uses a downward-facing frame.

The player holds an accepted leftward movement input during active gameplay while the character is not blocked → The character’s on-screen position shifts left and the character sprite uses a side-facing frame oriented left.

The player holds an accepted rightward movement input during active gameplay while the character is not blocked → The character’s on-screen position shifts right and the character sprite uses a side-facing frame oriented right.

The player holds accepted upward and leftward movement inputs together during active gameplay while both movement axes are unblocked → The character’s on-screen position shifts diagonally upward and left.
The player attempts to move upward into a blocking tile during active gameplay → The character remains outside the blocking tile and is shown adjacent to it while facing upward.
The player attempts to move upward outside the world boundary → The character remains inside the visible top world edge and does not enter any area beyond the map boundary.
The character’s movement destination overlaps a hole tile during active gameplay → The character begins a fall animation, moving toward the hole while the character sprite shrinks.
The character’s movement destination overlaps a water tile during active gameplay → The character begins a fall animation, moving toward the water while the character sprite shrinks.
The character takes non-lethal damage while not invulnerable → The character sprite flashes by alternating between its normal palette and a winter-colored palette in 200 ms visual intervals.

A damage event is applied while the player has one life unit remaining → The character enters a death sequence: the sprite repeatedly changes facing direction, then a fade overlay begins covering the gameplay view.

The character overlaps an active blade trap while not invulnerable → The character sprite begins the invulnerability flashing effect, alternating between its normal palette and a winter-colored palette.

The character overlaps a moving seeker trap while not invulnerable → The character sprite begins the invulnerability flashing effect, alternating between its normal palette and a winter-colored palette.

The character overlaps an active spike tile after the spike’s first animation frame while not invulnerable → The character sprite begins the invulnerability flashing effect, alternating between its normal palette and a winter-colored palette.
The character overlaps a spike tile on the spike’s first animation frame → The character does not begin the invulnerability flashing effect during that spike frame.
The character overlaps a skeleton enemy while not invulnerable → The character sprite begins the invulnerability flashing effect, alternating between its normal palette and a winter-colored palette.
The character overlaps a mommy enemy while not invulnerable → The character sprite begins the invulnerability flashing effect, alternating between its normal palette and a winter-colored palette.

The player performs the action input during active gameplay when a fireball launch is accepted and the character is facing upward → A fireball sprite appears at the character’s position and travels upward.

The player performs the action input during active gameplay when a fireball launch is accepted and the character is facing downward → A fireball sprite appears at the character’s position and travels downward.

The player performs the action input during active gameplay when a fireball launch is accepted and the character is facing left → A fireball sprite appears at the character’s position and travels left.

The player performs the action input during active gameplay when a fireball launch is accepted and the character is facing right → A fireball sprite appears at the character’s position and travels right.
A moving fireball reaches a blocking tile that is not destructible by fireball → The fireball sprite disappears at the blocking tile.
A moving fireball reaches a bush tile → The fireball sprite disappears and the bush tile disappears from the scene.
A moving fireball reaches a stone flower tile → The fireball sprite disappears and the stone flower tile disappears from the scene.
A moving fireball overlaps a skeleton enemy → The skeleton enemy disappears from the scene.
A moving fireball overlaps a mommy enemy → The mommy enemy disappears from the scene.
The player performs the action input with an inactive seeker trap below the character in the same unobstructed column → The seeker trap starts moving upward toward the character’s row.
The player performs the action input with an inactive seeker trap to the right of the character in the same unobstructed row → The seeker trap starts moving left toward the character’s column.

The player performs the action input with an inactive seeker trap in the same column and a blocking tile between the trap and the character → The seeker trap remains at its pre-action tile position and does not begin moving.

The player performs the action input with an inactive seeker trap in the same row and a blocking tile between the trap and the character → The seeker trap remains at its pre-action tile position and does not begin moving.
The player performs the action input with an inactive seeker trap that is not in the character’s row or column → The seeker trap remains at its pre-action tile position and does not begin moving.
A moving seeker becomes blocked during its movement animation → The seeker stops moving and is displayed aligned to a whole tile position instead of between tiles.
The player performs the action input with an inactive blade trap below the character in the same unobstructed column → The blade trap starts moving upward toward the character’s row.
The player performs the action input with an inactive blade trap to the right of the character in the same unobstructed row → The blade trap starts moving left toward the character’s column.

The player performs the action input with an inactive blade trap in the same column and a blocking tile between the trap and the character → The blade trap remains at its pre-action tile position and does not begin moving.

The player performs the action input with an inactive blade trap in the same row and a blocking tile between the trap and the character → The blade trap remains at its pre-action tile position and does not begin moving.
The player performs the action input with an inactive blade trap that is not in the character’s row or column → The blade trap remains at its pre-action tile position and does not begin moving.
A moving outbound blade trap reaches a blocking tile → The blade trap reverses direction from the blocking tile and travels back along its path.
A returning blade trap reaches a blocking tile during its movement animation → The blade trap stops moving and is displayed aligned to a whole tile position.
A skeleton enemy has an active movement direction and its next movement position is unblocked → The skeleton sprite shifts along its current movement direction.
A moving skeleton becomes blocked during its movement animation → The skeleton is displayed aligned to a whole tile position and then moves away from the blocking direction.
A mommy enemy has an active movement direction and its next movement position is unblocked → The mommy sprite shifts along its current movement direction.
A trigger tile advances its animation while at least two seasons are available → The trigger tile’s accent color changes to the color associated with another available season.
The player performs the action input while standing on a season trigger and a season change is available → A fade overlay begins covering the gameplay view as the season-change transition starts.
A season change completes for a season different from the current one → The gameplay background is redrawn to the newly selected season’s visual style.

The player performs the action input while touching the winter season orb → The touched orb sprite disappears from the map, the top-right heart display gains one heart icon compared with immediately before the input, and a black dialogue panel displays “IN WINTER, SNOW COVERS” and “AND WATER TURNS ICE” as two text lines.

The player performs the action input while touching the summer season orb → The touched orb sprite disappears from the map, the top-right heart display gains one heart icon compared with immediately before the input, and a black dialogue panel displays “IN SUMMER, ROOTS GROW” and “AND USE THE VINES TO CLIMB” as two text lines.

The player performs the action input while touching the fall season orb → The touched orb sprite disappears from the map, the top-right heart display gains one heart icon compared with immediately before the input, and a black dialogue panel displays “IN FALL, MUSHROOM GROW” and “AND LEAVES FILL HOLES” as two text lines.

The player performs the action input while touching the spring season orb → The touched orb sprite disappears from the map, the top-right heart display gains one heart icon compared with immediately before the input, and a black dialogue panel displays “IN SPRING, STONE FLOWERS” and “BLOOM” as two text lines.
A season orb is drawn in the world → The orb sprite is rendered using the color palette associated with that orb’s season.

A level is populated for a cat whose saved collection state is not collected → The cat sprite is displayed at its rescue position, and a sign panel is displayed at that cat’s collected corner position.

The player performs the action input while an uncollected cat is inside the interaction area → The cat is moved to its collected corner position and the sign panel at that collected corner disappears.
A fade transition is active during a rendered gameplay frame → A fade overlay is drawn over the entire game canvas, tinting or covering the visible scene underneath.

The gameplay view is rendered while the character is close enough to the left world edge that the camera offset is clamped → The world’s left edge is visible at the left side of the gameplay view, with no empty area outside the map shown to the left.

games.summaryZh: 生成一款第一人称环境线谜游戏：玩家探索紧凑场景、观察面板规则并绘制或连接正确路径，在逐步增加难度的谜题中获得重置、错误、解锁和完成反馈。

requirements.zh: The game has completed its initial page setup for the first level → The first puzzle level is shown in the gameplay view, with no title screen, menu screen, or curtain transition overlay visible.
A newly selected or advanced non-initial level enters its opening phase → A diagonal curtain overlay is drawn over the gameplay view during the level transition before the level is shown for play.
The current level is restarted after a failure or restart-triggering state → The level returns to its reset puzzle layout and a restart message overlay is shown over the gameplay view.
The reset control is released while it is enabled during a level → The current level returns to its reset puzzle layout, removing the player's drawn connections from the board.

The ending level is displayed → The text "Thank you for playing!" is shown near the upper part of the screen, and the text "But our princess is in another castle!" is shown near the lower part of the screen.
A non-final active puzzle reaches its solved state during running play → A diagonal curtain transition closes over the puzzle view.
The final regular level reaches its solved state during running play → After the transition, a level-select style screen is shown instead of another numbered regular puzzle level.
A connection is completed between two incompatible hotspots in a regular puzzle level → A restart message overlay appears over the gameplay view and the board returns to its reset puzzle layout.

A locked Coil level is selected from the level-select screen without Coil access enabled → A restart message overlay appears over the level-select view, and the level-select screen remains visible behind it without a curtain transition.

A selectable unlocked level exit is connected on the level-select screen after the level-select entry point is satisfied → A diagonal curtain transition begins, and the level-select view is replaced by the chosen level's puzzle board after the transition.
The level-select toolbar button is released while it is enabled during a level → A diagonal curtain transition closes over the current level before the level-select screen is shown.
A level with exactly two enabled toolbar buttons is displayed → The right-side toolbar shows two stacked buttons: a music button and a reset button.
A level with exactly three enabled toolbar buttons is displayed → The right-side toolbar shows three stacked buttons: a music button, a reset button, and a level-select button.
A current-level entry is displayed on the level-select screen → That level number is drawn in the light tile color used by the level-select highlight.
A completed non-current level entry is displayed on the level-select screen → That level number is drawn in gray.
An incomplete non-current level entry is displayed on the level-select screen → That level number is drawn in red.
A Coil entry is displayed on the level-select screen → The entry label begins with the text "Coil-" followed by its Coil level number.
A single-cell paint action is made on a grid cell that has an adjacent connected neighbor → The targeted cell changes to the neighboring connection's color.
During running play, the skull-turn timer selects an entry-point skull to turn → One entry-point skull changes its facing direction in the gameplay view.
A drawing stroke is made during running play in a reflected puzzle level → The stroke is drawn on the left side of the board and a mirrored matching stroke is drawn on the right side of the board.

A reflected puzzle level is displayed in its reset layout → The right half of the puzzle board is filled with a gray reflection-area background, while the left half shows the normal black board background outside tiles and hotspots.
A drawing stroke is requested while the level is not in its running phase → No new drawn connection or paint stroke appears on the puzzle board from that request.
A drawing stroke reaches the edge of the paintable puzzle bounds during running play → The visible paint stroke stops at the puzzle board edge and does not continue beyond the board.
A drawing stroke passes over an empty paintable cell during running play → The cell under the stroke changes from the background board color to the unconnected paint color.
A drawing stroke passes over an already connected paint cell during running play → The already connected cell keeps its connected color and no new unconnected paint mark is drawn over it.

A single-cell paint action is made on a grid cell that has no adjacent connected neighbor → The targeted cell changes to the unconnected paint color and no contiguous area fills with a connected color.
A new connection is completed between two compatible hotspots in a regular puzzle level → The connected painted path and the two compatible hotspots change to the connected paint color.
A drawing action adds new empty-cell paint in a level that contains fungus → At least one fungus-colored cell appears or changes within the fungus area after the paint is added.
A drawing stroke passes over a solid board tile during running play → The tile keeps its solid tile color and no paint mark appears on that tile.
A drawing stroke passes over a fungus cell during running play → The fungus cell keeps its fungus color and no paint mark appears on that cell.
An unsatisfied entry-point hotspot is displayed on a puzzle board → The hotspot's painted area is drawn in the entry-point color and a skull sprite is shown at that hotspot.
An unsatisfied exit-point hotspot is displayed on a puzzle board → The hotspot's painted area is drawn in the exit-point color and a grave sprite is shown at that hotspot.

The level-select screen is displayed → Selectable level labels are arranged along a curved arc, exactly three Coil labels are placed below the arc, and the title text "The Neatness" is shown near the lower part of the level-select view.
The first regular puzzle level is displayed → The instruction text "Connect the dots" is shown near the lower part of the gameplay view.
A level with moving skull guidance text is displayed → The instruction text "They move when you move" is shown near the lower part of the gameplay view.
A satisfied entry-point hotspot is displayed on a puzzle board → The hotspot remains marked by its skull sprite while its painted area is shown in the connected paint color.
A satisfied exit-point hotspot is displayed on a puzzle board → The hotspot remains marked by its grave sprite while its painted area is shown in the connected paint color.
The ending artwork is rendered with opacity at full value → A gray rectangular panel is shown near the center of the board with the princess sprite visible inside it.

games.summaryZh: 生成一款紧凑的三维第一人称射击游戏：玩家使用键鼠移动、跳跃、攻击并切换武器，在迷宫式关卡中与敌人交战，呈现弹药、生命、命中、伤害、武器和胜负状态。

requirements.zh: The game page has completed its initial UI setup before gameplay is started → A game canvas is shown with a centered title overlay displaying “Q1K3” and “CLICK TO START”.

The game canvas area is clicked while the initial “CLICK TO START” overlay is displayed → The centered start overlay is no longer shown, revealing the gameplay view with HUD areas at the screen edges.
Active gameplay is updating while the selected weapon does not require ammunition → The health HUD displays a numeric health value, and the ammo HUD displays “∞”.
Active gameplay is updating while the selected weapon requires ammunition → The health HUD displays a numeric health value, and the ammo HUD displays a numeric ammunition value.
The player presses jump while standing on the ground with jump re-enabled → The first-person viewpoint rises upward from its standing height.
The player looks upward to the vertical look limit → The view remains capped at the maximum upward pitch, and additional upward look input does not rotate the view beyond that capped angle.
The player looks downward to the vertical look limit → The view remains capped at the maximum downward pitch, and additional downward look input does not rotate the view beyond that capped angle.
The player scrolls to the next weapon after the mouse-wheel delay has elapsed → The visible held weapon model changes to the next available weapon.
The player scrolls to the previous weapon after the mouse-wheel delay has elapsed → The visible held weapon model changes to the previous available weapon.

The player attempts to fire a selected projectile weapon when the weapon is ready to shoot and has the required ammunition → A projectile is emitted from the player’s weapon during that firing attempt.

The player attempts to fire a selected muzzle-flash weapon when the weapon is ready to shoot and has the required ammunition → A muzzle-flash effect appears at the player’s weapon during that firing attempt.

The player attempts to fire a selected ammunition-using weapon when that weapon has zero ammunition and its reload wait has elapsed → No projectile or muzzle-flash effect is rendered for that firing attempt.
The player attempts to fire again before the selected weapon’s reload wait has elapsed → No new projectile or muzzle-flash effect is rendered for that firing attempt.
The player approaches a locked door while within the door activation range → A message reading “YOU NEED THE KEY...” is displayed over the gameplay view, and the door remains in its closed position.
The player approaches an unlocked door while within the door activation range → The door panel opens from its closed position, revealing the passage behind it.
An open door has had no player within its activation range for its reset delay → The door panel closes back toward its closed position.
The player collects the key pickup → The key pickup disappears from the scene and a message reading “YOU GOT THE KEY!” is displayed over the gameplay view.
The player collects a nail ammunition pickup while carrying the nailgun → The nail ammunition pickup disappears from the scene.
The player collects a grenade ammunition pickup while carrying the grenade launcher → The grenade ammunition pickup disappears from the scene.
The player reaches a non-final level exit trigger → The gameplay view switches from the current level layout to the next level’s map layout.

The player reaches the level-completion transition after the last available level → An end message is displayed with the heading “THE END” and the text “THANKS FOR PLAYING ❤”, and the visible health and ammo HUD text areas are blank.
The player’s health reaches zero from incoming damage → A centered overlay message reading “YOU DIED” is displayed over the gameplay view, and the health HUD shows 0.
The player death restart delay elapses → The current level is reloaded to its starting layout after the “YOU DIED” message has been shown.
A visible damageable entity’s health reaches zero from incoming damage → The entity’s original visible model is no longer rendered after the damage is applied.
An idle enemy has the player within its awareness range with an unobstructed line of sight → The enemy turns to face the player.
A patrolling enemy has the player within its awareness range with an unobstructed line of sight → The enemy turns to face the player instead of continuing along its patrol path.
An idle enemy receives nonlethal damage → The enemy turns to face the player and begins moving toward the player.
A patrolling enemy receives nonlethal damage → The enemy turns to face the player and begins moving toward the player instead of continuing its patrol path.
An idle enemy has the player outside its awareness range during its state update → The enemy remains in place and does not turn or move toward the player.
A patrolling enemy has the player outside its awareness range during its state update → The enemy continues along its patrol path and does not turn toward or move directly toward the player.
An idle enemy has the player within its awareness range but without an unobstructed line of sight during its state update → The enemy remains in place and does not turn or move toward the player.
A patrolling enemy collides horizontally with a wall or ledge boundary → The enemy reverses its patrol direction and walks back along its path.
A grunt enemy reaches its attack execution state while facing the player → A muzzle-flash light appears at the grunt during the attack.
A zombie receives a damage amount that is not above its gibbing threshold → The zombie model remains visible in its standing enemy form after the hit.

A visible bouncing entity collides vertically with a surface while its vertical speed is above its bounce threshold → The entity reverses vertical direction and rebounds away from the surface immediately after contact.

games.summaryZh: 生成一款键鼠操控的第一人称岛屿探索游戏：玩家在三维岛屿中移动和环视，发现资源、地点与环境线索，完成探索或生存目标，并通过 HUD、交互提示与场景变化获得明确反馈。

vlm.zh: A slow-enemies powerup timer is active during gameplay → A translucent blue overlay covers the gameplay view and visible enemies are drawn with a blue-tinted overlay.

replayTrace.zh: The weapon cooldown has completed during active gameplay while autofire is disabled, the mouse button is held, and triple shot is not active → One bullet line segment originates from the player ship and travels away from it.
The MENU button is activated from the paused screen and the return-to-menu confirmation is accepted → The game returns to the menu screen with the PLAY button visible.
The weapon cooldown has completed during active gameplay while triple shot is active → Three bullet line segments originate from the player ship in a spread pattern.

The gameplay view is first rendered for a newly reset run → The HUD SCORE value reads 000000, the PROGRESS bar has no filled segment extending from its left edge, and a level notification showing 01 is visible in the gameplay view.
The weapon cooldown has completed during active gameplay after the triple-shot powerup timer has expired and firing is accepted → Exactly one bullet line segment originates from the player ship.

vlm.zh: The Down movement input is held while the player ship is alive during active gameplay and the Up movement input is not held → The player ship's position shifts downward in the playfield on subsequent frames while the input remains held.

replayTrace.zh: The MENU button is activated from the paused screen and the return-to-menu confirmation is accepted → The game returns to the menu screen with the PLAY button visible.

The weapon cooldown has completed during active gameplay while autofire is disabled, the mouse button is held, and triple shot is not active → One bullet line segment originates from the player ship and travels away from it.

replayTrace.zh: A piercing bullet collides with its fourth distinct enemy during active gameplay → Hit particle effects appear at the enemy and the bullet line disappears after the impact.
The PLAY AGAIN button is activated on the game-over screen → The game-over screen is replaced by the active gameplay view for a new run.
The MENU button is activated on the game-over screen → The game returns to the menu screen with the PLAY button visible.
The weapon cooldown has completed during active gameplay after the triple-shot powerup timer has expired and firing is accepted → Exactly one bullet line segment originates from the player ship.
An air boss enemy is activated at the path entrance → A boss enemy appears at the path entrance with a 20 px square body, 6 px border, yellow air-colored accents, and an outer corner frame.
The player's last remaining life is lost → A browser alert dialog appears with the text “You lost.”.
The loss alert dialog is accepted → The game page reloads to the initial playfield view.
All waves have been sent and cleared while at least one life remains → A browser alert dialog appears with text beginning “You won! Based on lives and elemental fragments left, your score is:”.
The win alert dialog is accepted → The game page reloads to the initial playfield view.

The fifth wave is sent while the sixth wave remains queued → The wave display changes to “5 / 20”, and the next-wave preview counters show 0 earth enemies, 13 water enemies, 0 air enemies, and 0 fire enemies.

The tenth wave is sent while the eleventh wave remains queued → The wave display changes to “10 / 20”, and the next-wave preview counters show 0 earth enemies, 0 water enemies, 15 air enemies, and 0 fire enemies.

The fifteenth wave is sent while the sixteenth wave remains queued → The wave display changes to “15 / 20”, and the next-wave preview counters show 0 earth enemies, 0 water enemies, 0 air enemies, and 17 fire enemies.
The twentieth wave is sent as the final queued wave → The wave display changes to “20 / 20”, and the Send Wave control is displayed as disabled.

replayTrace.zh: An earth boss enemy is activated at the path entrance → A boss enemy appears at the path entrance with a 20 px square body, 6 px border, green earth-colored accents, and an outer corner frame.
The upgrade button is selected for a tower that is not upgradable → The tower upgrade/reclaim menu remains open, and the upgrade button remains shown as unavailable.
The player's last remaining life is lost → A browser alert dialog appears with the text “You lost.”.
The loss alert dialog is accepted → The game page reloads to the initial playfield view.
All waves have been sent and cleared while at least one life remains → A browser alert dialog appears with text beginning “You won! Based on lives and elemental fragments left, your score is:”.
The win alert dialog is accepted → The game page reloads to the initial playfield view.

vlm.zh: A leftward swipe steering input is accepted during active gameplay while the hero has an open path to the left → The hero moves leftward from its pre-input position along the playfield.
The hero collides with a 404 road-not-found sign during active gameplay while not being lane-redirected → A falling-road segment appears directly after the 404 sign on the road.

replayTrace.zh: A keyboard key release that does not match the next Konami-code key is accepted while the title screen is displayed before the Konami-code sequence is complete → The display changes from the title screen to the gameplay screen.
The gameplay screen is rendered during active play after the road map cache has been built → The gameplay viewport is filled by tiled highway lanes with shoulder tiles along the left and right edges.
A scheduled falling-road spawn becomes due and the new segment does not overlap a 200 road-OK marker → A new falling-road segment appears at the scheduled road position.

The hero overlaps a falling-road segment after that segment has passed the fatal animation frame during active gameplay → The hero is drawn rotated away from its upright orientation during a death animation.

The game has completed its initial page setup on a mobile device before gameplay is started → The title screen is visible with "js13kgames 2020" centered near the top, "collect teapots" centered above the middle, "for extra points" centered below it, "swipe to steer" centered below "for extra points", "jerome lecomte" centered near the bottom, and a highway scene behind the text with the hero sprite near the lower center.

vlm.zh: A fish on the belt with an attached paper ticket whose printed value matches that fish’s required score attempts scoring. → A check mark and orange ray particles appear around the fish, and the fish changes to a translucent appearance.

replayTrace.zh: A fish that is not on the belt but has an attached paper ticket attempts scoring. → No scoring particle burst appears around the fish, and the fish keeps its current opacity.

vlm.zh: The results screen is created after a level in which at least one fish spawned. → The results screen displays the spawned fish entries in a grid, with each row containing at most eight fish entries.

The results reveal animation reaches a fish entry that is marked correct. → The fish entry becomes visible in its results grid cell, a particle burst appears around that entry, and the results score counter’s displayed digits change during the reveal.

The results screen is created after a level with a nonzero maximum score. → The results screen shows a money line containing the current results score counter, a slash glyph, the maximum score counter, and currency signs; it also shows a percentage line containing a percentage counter and a percent sign.

replayTrace.zh: A held fish is dropped on a drop target that can host it while the paw is able to drop. → The fish is placed on the drop target, and the fish’s shadow is visible again.
The back button is activated on the results screen. → The results screen is replaced by the level-select screen through the tiled screen transition.

vlm.zh: A level-ending condition is reached during active gameplay on a built-in level that is not the final built-in level → The display changes from the gameplay board to the level selector screen, and the selection highlight is shown on the numbered level entry immediately after the completed level.

A level-ending condition is reached during active gameplay on the final built-in level → The display changes from the gameplay board to the level selector screen, and the selection highlight is shown on the first numbered level entry.

The gameplay UI is rendered while the performed-step count is 11 → The visible step counter text is drawn in yellow, and across consecutive gameplay frames the step counter text is drawn at changing horizontal or vertical positions while the level grid remains aligned.

The gameplay UI is rendered while the performed-step count is 12 → The visible step counter text is drawn in orange, and across consecutive gameplay frames the step counter text is drawn at changing horizontal or vertical positions while the level grid remains aligned.

The gameplay UI is rendered while the performed-step count is at least 13 → The visible step counter text is drawn in red, and across consecutive gameplay frames the step counter text is drawn at changing horizontal or vertical positions while the level grid remains aligned.

A movement command is processed during active gameplay when the destination contains a lock and the player has at least one collected key → The player character remains on its current tile facing the lock, and the lock tile shrinks during a removal animation until the lock is no longer visible.

A movement command is processed during active gameplay when the destination contains a lock and the player has no collected keys → The player character remains on its current tile facing the lock, and the lock tile remains visible in its grid cell.
A completed player movement leaves a trap tile and lands on a tile that is not a hole without performing a tile action → The trap tile the player just left changes into a hole tile.

A completed player movement lands on a spawn tile during active gameplay → The previous current-spawn tile changes to a regular spawn tile, the destination spawn tile changes to the current-spawn appearance, and the player character stands on the new current-spawn tile.

A completed player movement lands on a switch-trigger tile before the step limit is reached → Switch tiles with the same orientation as the trigger change between their switch-on and switch-off appearances.
A mouse-wheel orientation change is accepted on the level editor canvas → The orientation shown by the editor placement preview changes from its previous direction to another direction.
A right-button tile removal click is accepted on a filled grid cell in the level editor → The clicked editor grid cell changes to an empty grid cell.

A rightward option-change command is accepted on the “SELECT SKIN COLOR” character customization step → The selected skin-color swatch outline moves to a different swatch, and the character preview changes to that skin color.

A rightward option-change command is accepted on the “SELECT HAIR COLOR” character customization step → The selected hair-color swatch outline moves to a different swatch, and the character preview changes to that hair color.

A rightward option-change command is accepted on the “SELECT OUTFIT COLOR” character customization step → The selected outfit-color swatch outline moves to a different swatch, and the character preview changes to that outfit color.

replayTrace.zh: The highlighted Continue menu item is confirmed on the main menu while a saved current level is available → The display changes from the main menu to gameplay showing the saved level as the active board.
The level selector screen is rendered with at least one completed level entry → Each completed level entry shows a star tile on its preview.

The level selector screen is rendered when the completed-level list includes every numbered level → The level selector screen shows the level grid together with the texts “CONGRATULATIONS!” and “YOU ESCAPED ALL LEVELS WITHIN 13 STEPS!”.
A crate finishes moving onto a switch-trigger tile → Switch tiles with the same orientation as the trigger at the crate’s destination change between their switch-on and switch-off appearances.

A crate is pushed away from a tile that contains a switch-trigger underneath it → Switch tiles with the same orientation as the trigger under the crate change between their switch-on and switch-off appearances as the crate leaves that tile.

A crate is present on a switch tile that changes into the switch-on appearance during a switch inversion → The crate on that switch tile shrinks during a removal animation until the crate is no longer visible.
A crate finishes moving onto a switch-on tile → The crate shrinks during a removal animation until the crate is no longer visible on the switch-on tile.
A crate finishes moving onto a hole tile → The crate and the hole tile at that grid cell are replaced by a filled-hole tile.

A rightward movement command is processed during active gameplay when a pushable boulder is directly to the right of the player and at least one tile to the right of the boulder can receive it → The boulder moves right along its row until it reaches the last receiving tile before the next blocked tile or border, and the player character remains on its current tile facing right.

A movement command is processed during active gameplay when the destination contains a pushable boulder and the boulder has no receiving tile in the pushed direction → The player character remains on its current tile, and the boulder remains in its current grid cell.

A boulder finishes moving with an untriggered gong-trigger tile directly in front of its stopping direction → The gong tile with the same orientation as that gong-trigger shrinks during a removal animation until the gong is no longer visible.
A completed player movement leaves a switch-trigger tile → Switch tiles with the same orientation as the trigger change between their switch-on and switch-off appearances.

A rightward movement command is processed into a right-facing block-trigger tile during active gameplay → Block tiles connected from that trigger in the rightward direction shrink during removal animations until those blocks are no longer visible.

A movement command is processed into an untriggered gong-trigger tile during active gameplay → The gong tile with the same orientation as the gong-trigger shrinks during a removal animation until the gong is no longer visible.
The Test/Share control is accepted in the level editor while the edited level is valid → The display changes from the level editor to gameplay showing the edited level as a playable board.
The Test/Share control is activated in the level editor while the edited level is invalid → The display remains on the level editor, with the editable level grid still visible.
The menu background is rendered after its background image is available → A pixel-art background image is repeated horizontally across the visible canvas behind the menu screen.
The game completes initial setup with a valid encoded level parameter in the URL → The display opens directly to gameplay showing the decoded custom level as the active board.

An upward movement command is processed during active gameplay when the destination above the player contains a blocking tile that does not perform an action → The player character remains on its current tile and the character sprite faces upward.

A rightward movement command is processed during active gameplay when a pushable crate is directly to the right of the player and the tile one cell to the right of the crate can receive it → The crate moves one grid cell to the right, and the player character remains on its current tile facing right.

A completed player movement lands on a key tile during active gameplay → The key tile at the player’s destination disappears from the board while the player character remains on that destination tile.
The gameplay UI is rendered during an active built-in level → The UI shows text in the form “LEVEL: ” followed by the current level number, and the reset prompt “R: RESET” is visible.
A tile placement click is accepted on an empty grid cell in the level editor → The clicked editor grid cell changes to show the currently selected tile using the currently selected orientation.
The sound icon is clicked while the UI layer is rendered with sound enabled → The sound icon changes from the sound-on drawing to the muted sound-off drawing.
The sound icon is clicked while the UI layer is rendered with sound muted → The sound icon changes from the muted sound-off drawing to the sound-on drawing.

The initial menu screen has completed setup with no stored highscore available → A menu overlay is visible with a button labeled "Start", and the menu text shows the tip "Tip: Left click & drag to connect yurts to" followed by "farms, or delete paths with right click."

The Start button is accepted while the menu playfield is shown in its angled zoomed-in presentation → The menu overlay is no longer visible, and the main gameplay playfield is visible in an unrotated view.
The early active game reaches the score-counter reveal moment → The animal score counters are visible on the HUD.
The first active-game pond spawn chooses the large-pond branch and a valid position is available → A pond occupying a 6 by 4 cell area appears on the playfield.
A newly spawned farm with a predefined starting path reaches its delayed starting-path creation moment → A short visible path segment appears connected to the farm.

The fish-farm spawn opportunity occurs after the fish-farm threshold while no fish farm exists and a large pond is available → A fish farm appears on the pond with a visible stone path segment at the pond edge.

A new fish is added to the playfield → The fish counter area is visible, and the fish counter displays a number one greater than its displayed number before the fish was added.

The player attempts to fire a selected ammunition-using weapon when that weapon has zero ammunition and its reload wait has elapsed → No projectile or muzzle-flash effect is rendered for that firing attempt.
The player attempts to fire again before the selected weapon’s reload wait has elapsed → No new projectile or muzzle-flash effect is rendered for that firing attempt.

The player reaches a non-final level exit trigger → The gameplay view switches from the current level layout to the next level’s map layout.

The player reaches the level-completion transition after the last available level → An end message is displayed with the heading “THE END” and the text “THANKS FOR PLAYING ❤”, and the visible health and ammo HUD text areas are blank.
A patrolling enemy receives nonlethal damage → The enemy turns to face the player and begins moving toward the player instead of continuing its patrol path.
A patrolling enemy collides horizontally with a wall or ledge boundary → The enemy reverses its patrol direction and walks back along its path.
A visible damageable entity’s health reaches zero from incoming damage → The entity’s original visible model is no longer rendered after the damage is applied.
